findings.title: Any authenticated user can self-grant admin: profiles.is_admin is client-writable, defeating every is_admin(auth.uid()) gate in the schema
findings.detail: profiles.is_admin (added default false at 20260421000000_profiles_is_admin.sql:10-11) is the single source of truth for ALL privileged gating: the is_admin(uuid) helper reads only this column, and every admin RPC (glyph/domain/emotion/achievement moderation), all 8 analytics RPCs, the lab-assets storage writes, and unpublished-logs reads gate on is_admin(auth.uid()) in-body. But the profiles UPDATE policy is `for update using (user_id = auth.uid())` with NO `with check` clause, no column scoping, and no BEFORE UPDATE guard trigger on is_admin (the only profiles update triggers are set_updated_at, which only touches updated_at, and profiles_handle_guard, which fires only `of handle`). There is also no column-level privilege revoke on is_admin, so Supabase's default column grants to the authenticated role apply. Failure scenario: a signed-up user holding the publishable anon key sends a single PostgREST request PATCH /rest/v1/profiles?user_id=eq.<own-uid> with body {"is_admin": true}; RLS passes (they own the row, the implied WITH CHECK = USING still holds user_id=auth.uid()), the column is written, and the user is now a full operator. They can then read every user's analytics aggregates, approve/reject/re-price glyph submissions, approve their own submissions, mutate the emotion/domain/achievement catalogs, write to the public lab-assets bucket, and read unpublished logs. This is the same 'view/policy runs with more authority than the caller should have' class the repo already fixed twice (#442 v_ripple, #616 v_pebbles_full), now via a writable capability column. The pebble_drafts author even flagged the missing WITH CHECK on the core-table style (20260729213348:44-45) but reasoned only about user_id and missed is_admin entirely. Secondary consequences of the same root policy gap: max_media_per_pebble is self-writable (a user raises their own per-pebble media quota, bypassing the storage-cost guard), and terms_accepted_at/privacy_accepted_at are self-writable (a user can forge their own consent-proof timestamps, undermining GDPR accountability).
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260411000001_core_tables.sql:159-160 (profiles_update: `for update using (user_id = auth.uid())`, no with check); 20260421000000_profiles_is_admin.sql:10-11 (is_admin column) and :20-28 (is_admin() reads only this column); is_admin gate call sites e.g. 20260430000000_analytics_thin_slice.sql:87, 20260630084718_admin_glyph_moderation.sql:22, 20260421000003_lab_assets_bucket.sql:22-24; confirmed no later re-emission of profiles_update and no column privilege via grep over all migrations.
findings.remediation: Add a migration that either (a) recreates profiles_update with a `with check (user_id = auth.uid())` PLUS a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that raises if is_admin (and other privileged columns) changed without is_admin(auth.uid()) already true, or (b) revoke update on the is_admin/max_media_per_pebble columns from authenticated and mutate them only via a service-role/admin RPC. Prefer a guard trigger (pattern already used by profiles_handle_guard) that pins is_admin, max_media_per_pebble, terms_accepted_at, privacy_accepted_at to their OLD values on client updates. Add a negative-path assertion to a verify harness (self-PATCH is_admin must fail) and wire it into CI.

verification.note: Independently reproduced the full chain. (1) profiles.is_admin (boolean not null default false, 20260421000000:10-11) is the only input to is_admin(uuid), which reads solely p.is_admin (20260421000000:21-27); that helper gates every privileged path I sampled: analytics RPCs (get_kpi_daily 20260430000000:87 and siblings), glyph moderation approve/reject/re-price (20260630084718:22,60,88,117), domain/emotion/achievement admin RPCs, logs unpublished reads (20260421000001:46-56), and lab-assets storage writes (20260421000003:22-34). Those RPCs revoke from public/anon but keep the authenticated grant ('the is_admin guard does the gating'), so a self-granted admin can call them all. (2) profiles_update is defined once as `for update using (user_id = auth.uid())` with NO with check, no column scope (20260411000001:159-160); grep confirms no later drop/alter/re-emission of that policy and no revoke or column-level privilege change on profiles/is_admin. PostgREST exposes public (config.toml schemas=['public','graphql_public']); Supabase default table grants to authenticated therefore cover the is_admin column. The only BEFORE UPDATE triggers on profiles are set_updated_at (touches updated_at only) and profiles_handle_guard (`before update OF handle` — does not fire on an is_admin-only update). Postgres implies WITH CHECK = USING, so PATCH /rest/v1/profiles?user_id=eq.<own-uid> {\"is_admin\":true} passes both predicates on the caller's own row and persists. (3) Aggravating: the public_profiles migration author explicitly states 'profiles_update RLS lets owners write columns directly' (20260730120000:22-25) and for that exact reason guarded `handle` with CHECK constraints plus a dedicated before-update-of-handle trigger against direct client .update() bypasses (20260730120000:82-106); the pebble_drafts author also flagged the core-table UPDATE policy's missing with check (20260729213348:44-45). The team knew the write-bypass class and hardened handle, but is_admin got no CHECK, no trigger, no column revoke. Secondary claims verified: max_media_per_pebble (20260426000001:16) and terms_accepted_at/privacy_accepted_at (20260411000001:26-27) are plain profiles columns under the same unguarded policy and are self-writable. Impact 5 (single-request full-operator escalation: all-user analytics, self-approving glyph submissions, catalog mutation, public bucket writes, unpublished-log reads, forged consent timestamps) and likelihood 4 (any authenticated user; anon publishable key ships client-side; is_admin column name is in the committed database.ts and any `select *`) are honest. Severity 20 stands.

findings.title: Art. 9 processing rests on an explicit-consent gate that does not exist, and no DPIA is on record
findings.detail: The privacy policy qualifies moods, emotion labels, and CBT-style reflections as special-category health data and states they are processed only with explicit consent 'which you provide during onboarding'. No such consent step exists anywhere: onboarding is three intro screens (path/pebble/ritual) with no consent capture, and signup offers only generic terms/privacy checkboxes that never name the sensitive nature of the data. OAuth accounts get no consent record at all. No DPIA or Art. 9 memo exists in the repo despite the product's core activity being emotional-state journaling with social sharing features that enlarge the processing. The declared lawful basis for the product's central processing is therefore not evidenced by anything the system actually collects, which is exactly the accountability failure Art. 5(2), 7(1) and 9(2)(a) target.
findings.evidence: apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md:91-99 and 117-128 (explicit-consent claim); apps/web/lib/config/onboarding-steps.ts:8-12 (no consent step); apps/web/app/register/page.tsx:185-231 (generic checkboxes only); grep -ri 'dpia' docs/ apps/web returns only the quality-framework files
findings.remediation: Write and date a DPIA before the next feature enlarging sensitive processing; add an explicit consent step (naming emotional/health-adjacent data in user-facing language) to signup/onboarding on every path, persist it server-side alongside the existing timestamps, and add a settings withdrawal toggle whose effect the backend honors.

verification.note: Re-checked every cited artifact plus everything that could neutralize the claim. (1) apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md sections 3.2 and 4.2 state verbatim that moods/emotion labels/CBT reflections are Art. 9 special-category health data processed only with explicit consent 'which you provide during onboarding'. (2) apps/web/lib/config/onboarding-steps.ts defines exactly three steps (path/pebble/ritual) and components/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.tsx renders only a heading and body text per step; no consent capture exists in onboarding. (3) app/register/page.tsx has only generic terms/privacy checkboxes linking to the docs; neither names sensitive data, and acceptance is a signup precondition (submit disabled until checked), which cannot double as freely given, specific Art. 9 explicit consent. (4) The OAuth claim is corroborated by the repo itself: the Apple/Google buttons on the register page are gated only by `submitting`, not by the checkboxes, so a web OAuth signup records nothing, and migration 20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql line 11 states in its own comment that 'OAuth signups carry no consent metadata'; handle_new_user writes NULL timestamps for them. (5) Repo-wide grep for dpia/aipd/impact assessment hits only docs/quality framework criteria files (the audit rubric), never an actual DPIA, despite CNIL listing health-data processing among processing requiring one. Aggravating factors found beyond the finding: privacy policy section 4.3 promises consent withdrawal 'at any time via your profile' but no consent or withdrawal surface exists anywhere in apps/web/app/settings, app/profile, or components/profile; profiles.terms_accepted_at/privacy_accepted_at are written at email signup but never read or enforced by any gate, so even the generic record has no operational effect; and the store-launch roadmap (M55: 'Consent: F2 plus a re-consent surface') plans only generic re-consent, confirming the Art. 9 gate is known future work, not present. Severity 4x4 is honest: the gap applies to 100 percent of accounts of a live product whose core activity is the declared special-category processing, under CNIL jurisdiction, and Art. 9 has no contract-performance derogation to fall back on.

findings.title: Android ships zero crisis resources and answers maximum-negative entries with karma rewards and achievement celebrations
findings.detail: The Android client contains no crisis, helpline, support or resource string in any locale, and the recording flow's completion path is identical for every emotional state: after publishing a pebble the success step renders '+N karma' with a sparkle icon whenever the server returns a positive delta, with no branch on valence or intensity, and the karma flash (sound + haptic, described in-code as 'the celebration') fires on every create/enrich. Worse, the emotion_first achievement family means a user recording a deeply negative emotion for the first time - plausibly at their worst moment - is interrupted by a full-screen 'Achievement unlocked - First [Sadness]' celebration card. An emotion journal is disproportionately likely to be open during a crisis; this is the highest-severity UX failure the product class has, and it is also Play 'Health Content and Services' policy exposure for an app already auto-publishing to Play internal testing.
findings.evidence: grep -ril 'crisis|helpline|suicide' apps/android/app/src/main matches no source or resource file (only binary font/svg byte coincidences); apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/pbbls/android/features/path/record/steps/RecordSuccessStep.kt:91-110 (karma row, no valence branch); features/path/create/CreatePebbleScreen.kt:282 and features/path/EditPebbleScreen.kt:200 and features/path/record/RecordFlowScreen.kt:274 (valence-independent notifyEarned); features/karma/KarmaNotificationService.kt:41-44 (sound/haptic are the celebration); res/values/strings.xml:462,485-486 with features/shared/achievements/AchievementCopy.kt:41 (First-emotion celebration)
findings.remediation: Add a localized (en/fr) crisis-resources screen bundled statically, surface it within one interaction of a high-distress entry (e.g. on the success step when valence is lowlight at high intensity), suppress the karma/achievement celebration on that branch, and pin the branch with a screenshot test plus LocalizationParityTest coverage of the new keys.

verification.note: Re-checked every cited file plus server logic. (1) No crisis/helpline/suicide/hotline string exists in any Android source or resource (values or values-fr); repo-wide, the only mention is a prohibited-content clause in web terms. (2) RecordSuccessStep.kt:91-110 celebrates with sparkle + '+N karma' with no valence/intensity branch, and compute_karma_delta (20260411000003_rpc_functions.sql) starts at +1 with no valence input, so the celebration shows on literally every successful publish including maximum-negative entries. (3) Aggravating: sync_achievement_catalog auto-generates emotion-first badges for all 16 seeded emotions (sadness, anger, fear, shame, guilt, anxiety included); check_achievements unlocks on mere existence of one pebble with that emotion, ignoring intensity; Android fires the check after every publish (Success and SoftSuccess) in all three composers and on emotion-changing edits, and AchievementMomentOverlay is a full-screen scrim card ('Achievement unlocked' / 'First Sadness') with trophy, '+N karma' line and CONFIRM haptic drawn above the record-flow cover in RootScreen. Two evidence details are inexact but non-load-bearing: the default record flow passes presentsCapsule=false so notifyEarned early-returns (no capsule, no haptic there; the haptic capsule fires only on the fallback-form create and on enrich), and Android plays no sound at all ('sound' exists only in a comment ported from iOS). The Play pipeline (android-release.yml auto-publishing to internal testing on every main push) is real, though internal testing is limited distribution. The headline behaviors are deterministic for every user's first negative-emotion pebble, so 4x4 is honest.

findings.title: No age gate or server-recorded age assurance anywhere; GDPR Art.8 consent-age basis is undemonstrable for an intimate social product
findings.detail: The schema, auth trigger, and clients contain no age or birthdate field and no age attestation. grep of birth/date_of_birth/age/minimum_age across all migrations and types/database.ts returns nothing; handle_new_user_consent records only terms/privacy timestamps (20260729120000:17-28); grep of birth/age/dob across apps/ returns nothing. Any EU user, including a child below the applicable Art.8 threshold (13-16; France 15), can create an account with just an email or a federated login and immediately record intimate emotional content and use social features (connections, public profiles). Failure scenario: a 12-year-old signs up, is offered connection invites and a public profile, and the controller has captured no age basis and applied no minors-default matrix, so consent under Art.8 is invalid and the store target-audience/age declarations cannot be reconciled with the content. This is simultaneously a child-safety failure, an Art.8 consent defect, and a store-policy exposure at the store-launch milestone the roadmap is driving toward.
findings.evidence: grep age/birth/dob -> none in supabase/migrations, types/database.ts, apps/; 20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql:17-28; supabase/config.toml enable_signup=true; public_profile default false 20260730120000_public_profiles.sql:29 (not age-derived)
findings.remediation: Add a server-recorded age gate at signup (birthdate or over-threshold attestation persisted to profiles, refusing under-threshold accounts), map the enforced minimum to each served member state's Art.8 age, and if minors are admitted ship a private-by-default minors settings matrix (public profile off, discoverability off, no profiling). Commit store age/target-audience metadata and diff it in CI.

verification.note: Independently re-verified every evidence item: no birth/age/dob column in any migration or types/database.ts; handle_new_user (20260729120000:17-28) records only terms/privacy timestamps and its own comment concedes OAuth signups carry no consent metadata at all (NULL timestamps on federated logins); web register/page.tsx and Android AuthScreen.kt offer only terms+privacy checkboxes with OAuth buttons bypassing even those; iOS auth has nothing age-related; enable_signup=true; public_profile default false is a privacy opt-in, not age-derived. One evidence nuance that does not neutralize the claim: apps/web/docs/terms/en.md:87 and privacy/en.md:278-284 DO declare a 13+ minimum with France parental-consent rules, so the product is at declared-but-unenforced rather than fully silent, which is precisely the deficiency the finding describes and matches the repo's own quality framework's second-lowest maturity level for this criterion. Aggravating factor found: privacy policy 10.2 (en.md:284, fr.md:258) explicitly promises parental-consent confirmation "during sign-up" for 13-14-year-olds, but no signup flow on any surface asks it, making the published policy a documented misrepresentation on top of the missing gate. Impact 4 x likelihood 4 is honest for an unenforced age basis on 100% of signups of an intimate emotional product with social features at a store-launch milestone.

findings.title: No age gate exists on any signup path despite a declared 13+ minimum and a claimed parental-consent step
findings.detail: The terms declare a 13-year minimum with parental consent required for 13-15 in France, and the privacy policy states parental consent is confirmed during sign-up for ages 13-14. Nothing in the web signup or onboarding asks for a birthdate, an age attestation, or a parental-consent confirmation, and nothing is stored server-side. A 10-year-old can create an account recording emotional states and enable a public profile with the same defaults as an adult. The policy also accepts 13-14 with an (unimplemented) parental mechanism in France, where the Art. 8 consent age is 15, so even the declared posture is inconsistent with the served jurisdiction. The roadmap acknowledges this as an open blocker, but nothing has shipped.
findings.evidence: grep -ri 'birth|dob|age' over apps/web/app/register, apps/web/app/onboarding, apps/web/components/onboarding: zero age inputs; apps/web/docs/terms/en.md:87; apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md:280-284; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-store-launch-roadmap.md:25 ('no age gate (GDPR-K France = 15)')
findings.remediation: Add a birthdate or over-threshold attestation step to signup on every path, enforce France's 15-year Art. 8 threshold (or implement the verifiable parental-consent flow the policy promises), persist the evidence server-side, and align the policy text with what is actually enforced. Coordinate the same gate on iOS/Android.

verification.note: Independently re-verified every cited artifact. apps/web/app/register/page.tsx collects only email/password/confirm plus terms and privacy checkboxes; grep for birth/dob/age/minor/parental/consent across app/register, app/onboarding, and components/onboarding returns zero matches. No migration in packages/supabase/supabase/migrations defines any age or birthdate column (the only 'age' hits are the substring in storage_path), and handle_new_user() (20260729120000) inserts only user_id, display_name, and the two consent timestamps, so no server-side age record or guard exists. terms/en.md 3.1 declares the 13+ minimum with French 13-15 parental consent; privacy/en.md 10.2 affirmatively claims consent is confirmed 'during sign-up', which is false in code; the store-launch roadmap still lists 'no age gate (GDPR-K France = 15)' as an open blocker. The public-profile claim also holds: public_profile defaults false but is toggleable by any user with no age condition (20260730120000, settings/page.tsx), and get_public_profile is anon-granted so an enabled profile is world-readable. Aggravating: the Google/Apple OAuth signup paths bypass even the terms/privacy checkboxes, and the consent migration's own comment confirms OAuth signups carry no consent metadata at all; and 10.2 is a misstatement of current practice rather than a mere omission. Impact 4 x likelihood 4 is honest.

findings.title: No CI gate runs iOS tests or lint: every iOS change merges green-by-absence
findings.detail: The repo has 451 iOS unit tests and a SwiftLint config, but nothing executes either on pull requests. .github/workflows/ has jobs for Android, the Arkaik bundle, and lab notes only; the Xcode Cloud script provably covers build setup, not testing. A PR that breaks pebble decoding, draft hydration, or the publish soft-success recovery merges clean with zero checks, and the regression ships to the whole iOS user base at the next TestFlight/App Store build. This also voids the l4 ambitions of every other TST criterion on this surface: the suite's excellent quality protects nothing at merge time. The shared-contract hole is worse: a packages/supabase migration changing a shape iOS decodes triggers no iOS job either.
findings.evidence: ls .github/workflows/ = android.yml, android-release.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml (no iOS entry); ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh (build setup only, no xcodebuild test or swiftlint invocation); apps/ios/README.md:72 ('Builds on Xcode Cloud'); docs/quality/audits/2026-08/baseline.md:13 ('iOS has no GitHub Actions workflow'); apps/ios/package.json:8-9 defines the lint/test commands nothing in CI calls.
findings.remediation: Add a macOS-runner workflow (or an Xcode Cloud PR workflow with the test action) that runs 'npm run lint --workspace=@pbbls/ios' and 'xcodebuild test -scheme Pebbles' on pull_request with paths covering apps/ios/**, packages/supabase/**, and the workflow file itself; mark the job a required status check on main.

verification.note: Re-verified every evidence item: .github/workflows/ holds only android.yml, android-release.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml (grep of .github for xcodebuild/swiftlint/macos finds nothing executable); apps/ios/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh does only xcodegen install, Secrets.xcconfig write, project generation, and SPM resolution — no xcodebuild test and SwiftLint is never even installed on Xcode Cloud, so CI lint is impossible, not just unconfigured; apps/ios/README.md:72 and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-android-bootstrap-design.md:26 both describe Xcode Cloud as build-only; baseline.md:13 confirms no iOS GitHub Actions workflow; package.json lint/test scripts exist and are called by nothing in CI. The 451 test count is exact (sum of @Test annotations in PebblesTests), including the exact contract tests the finding cites (PebbleDecodingTests, DraftCrossSurfaceDecodingTests). The one theoretical neutralizer — a Test action configured in App Store Connect outside the repo — is contradicted by three in-repo docs and could not cover lint or fire on packages/supabase changes regardless. Aggravating: the repo's agent dev loop runs in a Linux container with no iOS toolchain (exit 127 per baseline.md), so PR authors often cannot run the suite locally either — merge-time coverage is the only possible gate and it is absent; the repo's own TST criterion (docs/quality/criteria/tst-testing-verification.md:271) counts hosted CI configs only if they run tests on PRs, which this provably does not. Severity 16 (4x4) is honest.

findings.title: No CI check of any kind runs on packages/supabase changes — migrations, RPCs, and RLS merge gateless
findings.detail: No GitHub Actions workflow references packages/supabase: grep of .github/workflows for 'supabase', 'migrations', or 'verify-' returns nothing, and the package's own lint script is a placeholder echo that exits 0. A PR that edits an RLS policy, re-emits a security-definer function, or ships a migration triggers zero automated checks and merges green by absence — on the one surface all four clients share. This is not hypothetical: two contract defects already landed through this hole in one month — the purge_account parallel re-emission collision that silently dropped the connections deletes (#687), and admin_set_domain_glyph carrying a reference to the dropped shape_id column for 28 days because plpgsql bodies are parsed but not name-resolved at creation time. Both were caught by manual reading, not by any gate. Even the cheap checks the repo already has (tsc --noEmit, deno check of edge functions, a supabase db reset apply-check of the migration chain) run nowhere on merge.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ contains only android.yml, android-release.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml; android.yml:9-16 path-filters to apps/android/** only; packages/supabase/package.json:9 (placeholder lint); docs/quality/audits/2026-08/baseline.md:11; incident evidence: packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260731090000_purge_account_union.sql:1-18 and 20260731090100_fix_admin_set_domain_glyph.sql:4-14
findings.remediation: Add a supabase.yml workflow path-filtered on packages/supabase/** that: (1) runs supabase start + db reset to prove the migration chain applies, (2) regenerates types and fails on git diff, (3) runs tsc --noEmit and deno check over supabase/functions and scripts, (4) optionally runs the anon-key harnesses against the local stack. Make it a required check.

verification.note: Re-checked every cited artifact. (1) /home/user/pbbls/.github/workflows/ contains exactly android.yml, android-release.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml; android.yml lines 7-16 path-filter to apps/android/** and .github/workflows/android.yml only; arkaik.yml filters to docs/arkaik/**; the only 'supabase' hits in workflows are SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY secrets baked into Android builds, not gates. (2) packages/supabase/package.json line 9: lint is literally "echo 'placeholder — no lint step yet'"; line 8 shows tsc --noEmit exists as the build script yet no workflow invokes it, and four edge functions (compose-pebble, compose-pebble-update, delete-account, backfill-pebble-render) exist with no deno check anywhere. (3) Both incident migrations exist and their headers confirm the finding verbatim: 20260731090000_purge_account_union.sql documents the parallel re-emission off base 20260729213348 where the by-timestamp winner silently dropped the three connections deletes, and 20260731090100_fix_admin_set_domain_glyph.sql documents the stale shape_id insert surviving from 20260703000000 (28 days after 20260701114205 dropped the column), found by manual reading while copying the function as a precedent. (4) docs/quality/audits/2026-08/baseline.md line by line matches. Neutralization search came up empty: no husky/pre-commit hooks, no prepare script, turbo.json defines no test task, and apps/web does not even declare @pbbls/supabase as a dependency (only apps/admin does), so even an indirect Vercel type-check gate could not catch SQL-body, RLS, or migration-collision defects — none of which surface in the committed database.ts anyway. Two aggravating factors: 19 of 63 migrations landed in July-Aug 2026 (high churn feeds the likelihood), and 37 migration files carry security definer functions, so the ungated surface includes the auth boundary and the GDPR deletion path (purge_account, delete-account). Two trivial imprecisions that do not move the score: lab-note-reminder.yml does technically trigger on every PR (but is advisory and inspects only the PR body, not code), and grep for 'supabase' in workflows returns the Android secret names (none gating). One mitigation confirmed: the purge_account regression never reached the linked project, per the fix migration header — but the admin_set_domain_glyph breakage did ship live and was latent for 28 days. Severity 4x4 is honest.

findings.title: The entire PebblesFont typography layer is fixed-size, so branded text ignores Dynamic Type across the app
findings.detail: Every one of the 21 PebblesFont tokens resolves to a fixed point size, and all six family helpers construct Font(UIFont(descriptor:size:)) from a literal CGFloat with no UIFontMetrics or relativeTo scaling. SwiftUI fonts built from UIFont this way do not respond to the user's text-size setting. The 81 pebblesFont call sites cover titles, button labels, the record-flow name input (Caveat 36pt), valence headline words (34-56pt), karma counters, meta rows, and card headings - so a low-vision user who raises the system text size gets larger system-styled body text next to permanently small branded text, and the most meaning-carrying copy (what the user is choosing, what a button does) never scales. Nothing verifies layouts at accessibility sizes either (no screenshot or UI tests; the parity audit records that no font-scaling pass has been done).
findings.evidence: apps/ios/Pebbles/Theme/Font+Pebbles.swift:105-127 (token-to-fixed-size map), 171-248 (helpers, no metrics scaling); grep 'UIFontMetrics|relativeTo:' over apps/ios/Pebbles excluding @ScaledMetric = 0 hits; 81 pebblesFont call sites (grep count); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-android-parity-audit.md:147
findings.remediation: Route every family helper through UIFontMetrics(forTextStyle:).scaledFont(for:) (map each token to its nearest UIFont.TextStyle), or rebuild tokens on Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo:); then walk the primary flows at the largest accessibility sizes and fix clipping (the valence lockup and record name input are the likely casualties).

verification.note: Independently re-read Font+Pebbles.swift: all token sizes are literal CGFloats (lines 105-127) and all six family helpers build Font(UIFont(descriptor:size:)) with no UIFontMetrics (lines 171-248), which SwiftUI renders at fixed size regardless of Dynamic Type. Re-ran the greps: zero UIFontMetrics/relativeTo font-scaling hits in apps/ios (only 9 @ScaledMetric container metrics), zero dynamicTypeSize/scaledFont overrides that could neutralize the claim, and exactly 81 pebblesFont occurrences across 35 files covering titles, button labels, the Caveat 36pt name input, 34-56pt valence words, karma counters, meta rows, and card headings. Verified the mixed-scaling scenario is real: Lab, Glyph, and badge views use system dynamic styles (.body/.footnote/.headline) that do scale next to the frozen branded text. Verified the absent safety net: apps/ios/CLAUDE.md says no UI tests, and the parity audit (line 147) records that no font-scaling pass has been done on either platform. Aggravating factor found: @ScaledMetric-driven container dimensions (52pt button heights, 44pt checkbox) DO scale with Dynamic Type while the pebblesFont labels inside them do not, so the mismatch appears within single controls, not just between adjacent text. Only nit: the enum has 22 token cases, not 21 - immaterial. Impact 3 x likelihood 5 is honest: deterministic for any non-default text size on nearly every screen.

findings.title: Apple and Google signup paths create accounts with no consent record at all
findings.detail: The email path collects two consent checkboxes and persists timestamps server-side, but both federated paths skip consent capture entirely. signInWithApple and signInWithGoogle create the account with only a passive one-line disclaimer beneath the buttons ('Read our Terms and Privacy before creating an account'), send no consent metadata, and the handle_new_user trigger therefore stores NULL consent timestamps for every OAuth account (the migration comment says so explicitly). The controller cannot demonstrate consent under Art. 7(1) for any Apple or Google signup, which is likely the majority path on iOS. There is also no document-version binding on the email path, so even those records cannot show which policy version was accepted.
findings.evidence: apps/ios/Pebbles/Services/SupabaseService.swift:92-141 (no consent data on either OAuth path); apps/ios/Pebbles/Components/Auth/LegalDisclaimerText.swift:12; packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql:11-12 ('OAuth signups carry no consent metadata'); packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260411000001_core_tables.sql:26-27 (timestamp columns only, no version column)
findings.remediation: Gate the Apple/Google buttons behind the same two checkboxes in signup mode (or an interstitial acceptance step on first OAuth sign-in), then persist acceptance server-side via an RPC after the session exists since signInWithIdToken carries no metadata. Add an accepted-version column alongside the timestamps and mirror the change on web and Android.

verification.note: Independently re-read all four cited locations plus surrounding context. SupabaseService.swift signInWithApple/signInWithGoogle send zero consent metadata; AuthView's consent checkboxes gate only the email submit button while the OAuth buttons are always active (disabled only by isSubmitting); WelcomeView exposes the same ungated OAuth buttons on the app's first screen with only the passive LegalDisclaimerText; the handle_new_user_consent migration's own comment admits OAuth signups carry no consent metadata, and ->> yields NULL so every OAuth profile stores NULL consent timestamps; profiles has timestamptz columns only, no document-version column, so even email-path records are not version-bound. Repo-wide grep confirms no neutralizing mechanism: no post-signin consent RPC, no onboarding consent step, no gate on NULL consent timestamps anywhere. Aggravating: the identical OAuth gap exists on web (useSupabaseAuth.ts:162-176) and Android (SupabaseService.kt email-only consent), and the repo's own GDP-01 criterion sets default impact 4/5, so impact 3 is below the criterion's own default. Likelihood 5 is deterministic (every federated signup lacks the record). Severity 15 is honest, arguably conservative.

findings.title: Apple and Google signup paths create accounts with no consent record at all
findings.detail: The register page requires the terms and privacy checkboxes only for the email path; the OAuth buttons on the same page (and on the login page, which also creates first-time accounts) invoke signInWithOAuth without checking the boxes and without sending any consent metadata. The handle_new_user trigger is deliberately NULL-safe for this case, so every OAuth-created profile carries NULL terms_accepted_at and privacy_accepted_at permanently, with no post-OAuth capture screen to repair it. Under real usage a large share of accounts (OAuth is typically the majority path) has no lawful-basis evidence whatsoever, defeating the purpose of the consent-persistence fix shipped in issue #617.
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/register/page.tsx:99-119 (handlers ignore checkbox state); apps/web/app/login/page.tsx:87,98; apps/web/lib/data/useSupabaseAuth.ts:159-177 (no metadata in signInWithOAuth); packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql:11-12 ('OAuth signups carry no consent metadata')
findings.remediation: Gate the OAuth buttons on the same checkboxes (persisting acceptance client-side through the redirect) or add a one-time post-OAuth consent interstitial that writes the timestamps to the profile; backfill NULL rows by prompting at next login.

verification.note: Re-read all four cited locations plus everything that could neutralize the claim. Confirmed: register page gates only the email submit on the checkboxes (page.tsx:78-81,242) while the OAuth handlers (99-119) ignore them and the OAuth buttons are disabled only by `submitting`; login page (84-104) exposes the same handlers with no consent UI, and Supabase OAuth creates accounts on first sign-in; useSupabaseAuth.ts:159-177 passes only provider+redirectTo (signInWithOAuth has no metadata option); the handle_new_user trigger casts absent metadata keys to NULL and its own comment says 'OAuth signups carry no consent metadata'. Verified no repair path exists: repo-wide grep shows terms_accepted_at/privacy_accepted_at written only in the email register(); onboarding components contain zero legal/consent references; the auth callback route's fallback even inserts profiles with only user_id+display_name. Aggravating: the web OAuth buttons carry no 'By continuing you agree' microcopy at all (checked en.json auth strings), so there is not even a clickwrap argument, unlike iOS which at least renders LegalDisclaimerText; and the gap is cross-surface (iOS signInWithIdToken/hosted OAuth and Android signInWith(Google) also send nothing, with an Android comment acknowledging it). Severity 15 (3x5) is honest: every OAuth signup deterministically produces a NULL-consent profile.

findings.title: No report primitive exists in the database contract while cross-user UGC is live, leaving every client unable to ship the store-required report pillar
findings.detail: The schema ships three cross-user content paths (connection-visible and public pebbles with free-text name and description, marketplace glyphs, public profiles) but contains no reports table, no report RPC, and no moderation queue for user-flagged content; the only review apparatus is pre-publication admin review of marketplace glyphs. Apple 1.2 and Play's UGC policy require an in-product reporting mechanism wired to an operator queue, and store review checks for its visible presence. Because the database is the contract for all four surfaces, no client can ship a report button until the server primitive exists, so the gap is structural, not a per-client omission. Failure scenario: iOS or Android submits for review with share links, connections, and the glyph market live; the reviewer flags missing UGC apparatus and rejects the build, or the app is removed post-launch after a complaint. The purge_account comment already anticipates a reports table (it names 'reports' in its future-tables list), confirming the primitive is known-missing rather than out of scope.
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/types/database.ts:42-1589 (full table list, no reports table); packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260817130000_pebble_visibility_grades.sql:64-79 and :99-131 (cross-user and anon read paths); 20260630084718_admin_glyph_moderation.sql:1-52 (glyph-only review queue); 20260729201326_account_deletion_purge.sql:28 (comment naming 'reports' as future); grep 'report' across apps/web/components, apps/web/app, apps/ios/Pebbles/Features, apps/android/app/src/main found no report UI
findings.remediation: Add a reports table (reporter, target kind + id, reason, status) with an insert RPC granted to authenticated, an is_admin-gated queue read RPC following the admin_list_glyph_submissions pattern, extend purge_account plus verify-account-purge.ts in the same change per the standing rule, then wire report UI on each client screen that renders cross-user content.

verification.note: Independently re-verified every evidence item at the audited code state (HEAD differs only by 4 docs commits). The full table and RPC lists in packages/supabase/types/database.ts contain no reports table and no report/flag RPC; the only moderation apparatus is pre-publication glyph review (20260630084718: admin_list_glyph_submissions/approve_glyph/reject_glyph). Cross-user UGC paths are live in the contract: 20260817130000 grants any authenticated user read of public pebbles and connections read of private ones via pebbles_select RLS, and get_shared_pebble projects free-text name/description to anon by share link; get_public_profile and the glyph market exist. The purge_account migration comment (20260729201326) names reports as a known future table. Independent grep of iOS/Android/web found no report UI (only WobbleFlags/crash-comment false positives). Aggravating factor the auditor did not cite: the repo's own store-launch roadmap (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-store-launch-roadmap.md) lists 'no in-app report/block for UGC (Apple 1.2)' under confirmed store compliance blockers and plans the exact missing primitive in milestone M56 (content_reports table, report affordances on marketplace glyphs/public profiles/public pebbles, admin moderation queue), and the decisions log defers handle-impersonation abuse handling to 'M56 adds reporting' — the project itself classifies this gap as launch-gating. Impact 5 is therefore corroborated by the repo's own launch-gate classification; likelihood 3 is honest since M56 is sequenced before store submission (M57) but is unbuilt, UGC already reaches real testers via Play internal testing, and no filtering apparatus exists either. Minor phrasing overreach (a client could ship a minimal email-based report affordance without a DB primitive) does not change the severity: the repo's own compliance plan requires the DB-backed queue, and today no report mechanism of any kind exists on any surface.

findings.title: Stored XSS: user-controlled glyph stroke `d` is interpolated raw into server-composed render_svg and injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML on anonymous and cross-user surfaces
findings.detail: glyphs.strokes is jsonb with no CHECK constraint and is user-writable through PostgREST under glyphs_insert RLS (`user_id = auth.uid()`), so an authenticated attacker can PATCH/POST arbitrary stroke objects with the publishable key. The edge compositor builds render_svg by string-interpolating each stroke `d` verbatim into an SVG (glyph.ts:255) and writes it to pebbles.render_svg (compose-and-write.ts:122). A `d` value such as `M0 0"/>
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/supabase/functions/_shared/engine/glyph.ts:255; packages/supabase/supabase/functions/_shared/compose-and-write.ts:122-128; apps/web/components/connections/ConnectionPebbleTile.tsx:41; apps/web/components/shared-pebble/SharedPebbleView.tsx:56; apps/web/components/pebble/PebbleVisual.tsx:84; apps/web/components/path/PathStone.tsx:132; packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260411000001_core_tables.sql:45,190; glyphs_insert RLS at same file
findings.remediation: Sanitize at composition: parse and re-emit each stroke `d` from a numeric path grammar (reject any character outside the SVG path token set) inside createGlyphArtwork before interpolation, so nothing but path data can survive. As defense in depth, run render_svg through a server-side SVG sanitizer (allowlist of elements/attributes) before write-back, and/or DOMPurify(svg,{USE_PROFILES:{svg:true}}) at every dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink that renders render_svg. Add a hostile-input fixture (a glyph whose `d` contains an attribute breakout) to the pebble-visibility/compose harness and assert the stored render_svg is inert.

verification.note: Independently reproduced the full stored-XSS chain end to end. SOURCE: glyphs.strokes is jsonb with no CHECK (core_tables.sql:45) and glyphs_insert/update RLS is bare user_id=auth.uid() (lines 190-193), so an authenticated attacker writes arbitrary stroke.d via PostgREST or via create_pebble's inline new_glyph path (visibility_grades.sql:167-175, which also sets attacker-controlled view_box to satisfy the "0 0 200 200" gate at compose-and-write.ts:76). No marketplace approval: can_use_glyph passes for an authored glyph. SINK: glyph.ts:255 interpolates d="${stroke.d}" with no escaping; I hand-traced the payload M0 0"/>

findings.title: Google sign-in button label is illegible in dark theme (themed foreground on fixed white)
findings.detail: GoogleSignInButton paints a fixed Color.White capsule but colors its 'Continue with Google' label with system.foreground, which flips to #E9E2E4 in dark theme. Light gray on white yields a contrast ratio of about 1.3:1, far below the 4.5:1 AA minimum and practically invisible. Every user with system dark mode who reaches Welcome or the Auth screen hits this on the primary sign-in affordance. The defect is faithfully ported from the identical iOS implementation (foregroundStyle(Color.system.foreground) on a white capsule), so the 1:1 mirror rule propagated a contrast bug to both store apps; fixing it means pinning the label to the light-theme foreground value (or a dedicated on-white token) on both platforms.
findings.evidence: apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/pbbls/android/components/GoogleSignInButton.kt:49 (.background(Color.White)) and :64 (color = system.foreground); theme/Palettes.kt:41 SystemPaletteDark.foreground = Color(0xFFE9E2E4); used at WelcomeScreen.kt:185 and AuthScreen.kt:228; same pattern in apps/ios/Pebbles/Components/GoogleSignInButton.swift
findings.remediation: Give the label a fixed dark ink (the light palette foreground 0xFF4A3639, or introduce an onWhite token) instead of the theme-flipping system.foreground; apply the same one-line fix to the iOS component and add a dark-mode screenshot preview of the auth screen.

verification.note: Re-read all cited code. Android GoogleSignInButton.kt paints a fixed Color.White capsule (line 49) and labels it with system.foreground (line 64); SystemPaletteDark.foreground is 0xFFE9E2E4 (Palettes.kt:41). PebblesTheme resolves the palette solely from isSystemInDarkTheme(), MainActivity wraps the whole tree in it, and no night-mode pin, forced-light wrapper, or palette override exists anywhere between the theme root and the two call sites (WelcomeScreen.kt:185, AuthScreen.kt:228). Independently recomputed the contrast: #E9E2E4 on white is about 1.28:1, failing WCAG AA 4.5:1; in dark mode the label color equals light mode's muted border token. iOS mirror confirmed with one trivial citation slip: the file is Components/Buttons/GoogleSignInButton.swift (not Components/), but it has the identical pattern (.foregroundStyle(Color.system.foreground) on Capsule().fill(Color.white)) and the SystemForeground asset's dark appearance is the same 0xE9E2E4; no UIUserInterfaceStyle pin, preferredColorScheme only in previews. Aggravating: Android screenshot CI is render-to-view (references git-ignored, nothing fails on visual change) and the Compose preview default palette is SystemPaletteLight, so tooling systematically renders the legible light version and masks the bug. Mitigation already priced into impact 3: the white capsule and multi-color G glyph stay visible, so the affordance is discoverable by shape and logo even though the label is illegible. Severity 3x4=12 is honest.

findings.title: Primary and destructive token pairs fail WCAG AA in four of five light color worlds; primary button text lands at 2.97:1 in the default theme
findings.detail: The default Button variant renders text-primary-foreground on bg-primary at text-sm (components/ui/button.tsx:13), and that pair measures 2.97:1 in the default blush-quartz light world, 2.99 in moss-pool, 3.18 in cave-pigment, and 4.14 in dusk-stone, all below the 4.5:1 requirement for normal-size text and three of them below even the 3:1 large-text bar. The same primary color used as link text (link variant, text-primary) measures 2.99-4.14 on its world backgrounds. Destructive pairs measure 4.13-4.47 in light worlds and 2.77 in stoic-rock dark, and muted-foreground on muted sits at 4.10-4.38 in four dark worlds. Low-vision users cannot reliably read the main call-to-action labels, and no measurement exists in the repo to catch this class of failure.
findings.evidence: Ratios computed exactly from the hex tokens in apps/web/app/globals.css (blush-quartz :root lines 65-99: --primary #C07A7A vs --primary-foreground #F8F0F0 = 2.97; .moss-pool lines 389-424 = 2.99; .cave-pigment lines 227-262 = 3.18; .dusk-stone lines 308-343 = 4.14; .stoic-rock.dark destructive pair lines 203-204 = 2.77); consumer at components/ui/button.tsx:13 and :22 (link variant).
findings.remediation: Darken --primary (or lighten/darken --primary-foreground) per world until every primary and destructive pair clears 4.5:1, retune the dark-world muted-foreground values, then commit the contrast script used here (a small node/python pass over globals.css) as a CI check that fails on any pair below threshold.

verification.note: Recomputed every cited ratio from the hex/oklch tokens in apps/web/app/globals.css using an independent WCAG calculator (oklch converted per CSS Color 4, validated against the known 4.54 pair #767676/#FFFFFF): primary pairs 2.97/2.99/3.18/4.14 in blush-quartz, moss-pool, cave-pigment, dusk-stone (stoic-rock light passes at 17.16), link text 2.99-4.14, destructive light pairs 4.13-4.47 with stoic-rock dark at 2.77, muted-foreground on muted 4.10-4.38 in four dark worlds. All match the finding to the hundredth. Verified the pair is live: button.tsx bakes text-sm font-medium (14px/500, normal text so 4.5:1 applies), the failing combo is the default variant used by roughly 50 no-variant Button call sites plus badge.tsx, calendar.tsx, SoulPicker.tsx; blush-quartz is the :root default world so the 2.97:1 CTA is what every default light-mode user sees. Both cited files are byte-identical between commit 10181916 and HEAD, and grep confirms no contrast/axe/pa11y/lighthouse tooling anywhere in the repo. Aggravating: the actual destructive button variant (text-destructive on bg-destructive/10 composited over each world background) measures 3.48-3.99 across all five light worlds, failing even stoic-rock, the one world whose primary pair passes. Severity 3x4 is honest; likelihood is arguably 5 since the failure is unconditional in the default configuration.

findings.title: Vercel hosts the admin back office but is absent from the processor inventory and has no region pinning
findings.detail: Root CLAUDE.md states web and admin deploy to Vercel, yet the privacy policy's Art. 28 processor inventory lists only Supabase and Google Gemma. Every admin page render and server action passes personal data (submitter and owner emails from admin_list_glyph_submissions, aggregate special-category analytics, operator session cookies) through Vercel's serverless runtime. No region configuration exists anywhere: apps/admin has no vercel.json at all and apps/web/vercel.json contains only a $schema key, so functions run in Vercel's default US region (iad1) unless someone changed it in the dashboard, which the repo cannot demonstrate. That is EU personal data processed by an unlisted processor with no documented Chapter V transfer mechanism, under ordinary conditions on every request.
findings.evidence: Root /home/user/pbbls/CLAUDE.md ('Web and admin deploy to Vercel'); apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md:159-176 (inventory lists Supabase + Google only); find for vercel.json returns only apps/web/vercel.json whose sole content is the $schema key; apps/admin/next.config.ts is empty; admin_list_glyph_submissions emails at packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260701102810_glyph_marketplace_curation.sql:189-191
findings.remediation: Add a vercel.json with an EU regions key (e.g. cdg1/fra1) to apps/admin and apps/web, add Vercel to the processor inventory with its DPA reference and the transfer mechanism for any residual US processing, and remove the unused Google Gemma entry or mark it prospective.

verification.note: Independently re-verified every evidence point: (1) admin deploys to Vercel per apps/admin/README.md, the 2026-04-26 back-office spec, and packages/supabase/CLAUDE.md ("web/admin Vercel deploys"), not just root CLAUDE.md; (2) the only vercel.json in the repo (apps/web) contains solely a $schema key, apps/admin has none, apps/admin/next.config.ts is an empty config, and no preferredRegion/regions/runtime export exists anywhere in apps/admin, so no repo-demonstrable region pinning; (3) the Art. 28 inventory in both apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md (sec. 6, lines 159-176) and fr.md (sec. 6) lists only Supabase and Google, and "vercel" appears nowhere in apps/web/docs; (4) admin_list_glyph_submissions (migration 20260701102810) returns su.email/ou.email from auth.users, and the moderation page is an async Server Component calling it through createServerSupabaseClient (cookies from next/headers), so end-user emails, operator session cookies, and analytics RPC responses are processed in the Vercel function runtime on every render. Aggravating factors found: the policy affirmatively claims "No transfer outside the EU is involved in primary storage" (7.1) and "No transfer to external CDNs" (7.3) while all traffic transits Vercel's US-operated global edge, making the notice misleading rather than merely incomplete; the repo's own gdp-06 template cites the Vercel DPA, showing the framework anticipated Vercel as a processor; the policy still cites the invalidated Privacy Shield. Vercel's automatic DPA/DPF certification may supply a contractual Chapter V mechanism, but GDP-06 requires a documented one and a complete inventory, which the finding correctly states is absent. Severity 3x4 is honest.

findings.title: Google OAuth signup on Android creates accounts with no consent record, and stored consent is version-less
findings.detail: The email signup path collects and persists both consent timestamps, but signInWithGoogle passes no consent metadata, and both the Welcome screen and the Auth screen expose the Google button without requiring the checkboxes (they are only rendered in email SIGNUP mode). The server trigger explicitly NULL-safes the absent keys, so every Google-created account carries NULL terms_accepted_at/privacy_accepted_at forever - the controller cannot demonstrate consent (Art. 7(1)) for the entire OAuth cohort. Additionally the stored record binds no document version (the policy carries version 1.0.0 in frontmatter but the consentMetadata payload is two timestamps only), so a future policy change cannot trigger re-acceptance, and no age assurance exists on any path.
findings.evidence: apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/pbbls/android/services/SupabaseService.kt:183-190 (no data block on Google path) vs :159-173,249-253 (email path); features/auth/AuthScreen.kt:186-203 (checkboxes only in SIGNUP mode) and :228 (Google button gated only on isSubmitting); RootScreen.kt:273-276 (Google reachable straight from Welcome); res/values/strings.xml:18 (browsewrap disclaimer); packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql:11-12,26-27 (OAuth rows persist NULL)
findings.remediation: After a first OAuth session with NULL consent on the profile, block app use behind a consent interstitial that records timestamps plus the accepted document version via an RPC; add the version to consentMetadata on the email path in the same change.

verification.note: Re-checked every cited location and the surrounding guards; all hold. (1) SupabaseService.kt:183-190: signInWithGoogle() calls client.auth.signInWith(Google) with no data block, while signUp (:159-173) attaches consentMetadata() (:249-253, two timestamps only, no version key). (2) AuthScreen.kt: the two PebblesCheckbox rows render only under `if (mode == AuthMode.SIGNUP)` (:186-203) and AuthLogic.canSubmit enforces them only for the email submit button; GoogleSignInButton (:228) is gated solely on !isSubmitting, and runGoogle() (:116-128) never reads the checkbox state. (3) RootScreen.kt:270-276: WelcomeScreen wires onGoogleSignIn directly, and WelcomeScreen has no checkboxes at all, only LegalDisclaimer. (4) strings.xml:18 is "Read our {terms} and {privacy} before creating an account with Google" — weaker than a by-continuing clickwrap; no acceptance act. (5) Migration 20260729120000: `->>` casts yield NULL for absent keys (the comment itself states "OAuth signups carry no consent metadata"), and the one-shot backfill only recovers from raw_user_meta_data, which OAuth users never carry — so the OAuth cohort has no recovery path. (6) Version binding: apps/web/docs/{terms,privacy}/en.md carry `version: 1.0.0` frontmatter but profiles stores only two timestamptz columns; even email-path consent cannot be tied to a document version. (7) No age assurance anywhere in the funnel; the store-launch roadmap (M55) confirms the age gate and a re-consent surface are planned, unshipped work. No neutralizing guard exists: Android onboarding captures no consent post-OAuth, and no server-side check blocks NULL-consent profiles. Aggravating: the identical gap exists verbatim on web (register/page.tsx:281 Google button disabled only on `submitting`; useSupabaseAuth.ts signInWithOAuth passes no metadata, Apple path included) and iOS (SupabaseService.swift:125-141), so the NULL-consent cohort spans all surfaces and the migration comment institutionalizes rather than flags it. Mildly tempering: Android currently ships only to Play internal testing, so today's Android cohort is small — but android-release.yml auto-publishes on every main push and the severity (3x4) already reflects an accountability defect rather than a data leak, so 12 is honest.

findings.title: The Art. 9 explicit-consent gate the privacy policy promises does not exist in the shipped Android signup or onboarding, and no DPIA is on record
findings.detail: The controller's own policy declares moods and emotion labels special-category health data processed 'only with your explicit consent, which you provide during onboarding'. The shipped Android product has no such consent: signup shows two generic checkboxes referencing the Terms and Privacy Policy without naming emotional or health-adjacent data, and onboarding is a feature carousel with no consent step. The product therefore processes what it itself qualifies as Art. 9 data on a consent basis it never collects, for every account. No DPIA or Art. 9 memo exists anywhere in docs/ despite systematic emotional-state recording being an Art. 35(3)(b) trigger. The gap is documentary and structural rather than a leak (no telemetry SDKs exist on Android), but it converts the policy's own framing into evidence against the controller.
findings.evidence: apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md:92-97 ('explicit consent, which you provide during onboarding'), :117-127 (Art. 9 qualification); apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/pbbls/android/features/auth/AuthScreen.kt:186-203 (generic consent only); features/onboarding/OnboardingSteps.kt (carousel, no consent); grep -ril 'DPIA' docs/ matches only docs/quality/* framework files
findings.remediation: Write the DPIA against the current feature set; add explicit-consent copy naming the emotional/health-adjacent nature of the data to the signup/onboarding flow on every path and persist that acceptance server-side; or re-found the processing on a defensible alternative basis documented in a lawful-basis map.

verification.note: Independently re-read every cited artifact and hunted for neutralizing mechanisms. The policy citations are verbatim accurate: apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md sec. 3.2 and 4.1-4.3 qualify moods/emotion labels as Art. 9 health data processed 'only with your explicit consent, which you provide during onboarding.' AuthScreen.kt:186-203 shows exactly two generic checkboxes ('I accept the Terms of Service' / 'I accept the Privacy Policy' per strings.xml:28-30) with no health or special-category language anywhere in either locale's strings. OnboardingSteps.kt/OnboardingScreen.kt is a four-step marketing carousel whose Skip and close buttons both finish it from any page, so it structurally cannot collect consent, and no consent step exists in web or iOS onboarding either. The only consent machinery in the stack (migration 20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql + SupabaseService.consentMetadata) persists generic terms/privacy acceptance timestamps, which does not constitute a separate explicit Art. 9 act and does not rescue the false 'during onboarding' claim. DPIA greps (DPIA, AIPD, Art. 35, impact assessment, analyse d'impact) match only the audit framework's own criterion files. Aggravating factors found: Google OAuth signups record no consent metadata at all (the migration comment says so; the welcome screen is browsewrap only), and the policy's promised in-profile consent withdrawal (sec. 4.3/9.7) has no implementation in SettingsScreen.kt beyond full account deletion. Severity 12 is honest, if anything conservative given the gap holds for 100% of accounts.

findings.title: The iOS app ships no PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy privacy manifest
findings.detail: No privacy manifest file exists anywhere under apps/ios, yet the app uses UserDefaults via @AppStorage, which is a required-reason API (category NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults, reason CA92.1). Apple has enforced manifest declarations at submission since May 2024; a binary using listed APIs without declarations draws ITMS-91053 rejections, and the app-level manifest is also where collected-data types must be declared for an app whose whole purpose is collecting emotional data. The third-party SDKs (supabase-swift, SVGView, RiveRuntime) may bundle their own manifests, but the app target's manifest is the developer's responsibility and is absent.
findings.evidence: find /home/user/pbbls/apps/ios -iname '*xcprivacy*' returns nothing; apps/ios/Pebbles/RootView.swift:25 (@AppStorage 'hasSeenOnboarding' uses UserDefaults, a required-reason API); apps/ios/project.yml:38-69 (no manifest resource declared for the Pebbles target)
findings.remediation: Add PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy to Pebbles/Resources declaring NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults with reason CA92.1, the collected data types (emotional/journal content, contact info for account, photos, identifiers), and no tracking. Reference it in project.yml so xcodegen includes it, and mirror one into the widget target.

verification.note: Re-checked independently: (1) repo-wide find (not just apps/ios) confirms zero *.xcprivacy files and zero references to xcprivacy/NSPrivacyAccessed anywhere, with no script generating one; (2) apps/ios/Pebbles/RootView.swift:25 does use @AppStorage("hasSeenOnboarding"), i.e. UserDefaults (NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults, reason CA92.1) in the app's own code, so the symbols land in the main app binary and third-party SDK manifests cannot cover it; (3) project.yml:38-69 declares no manifest and Pebbles/Resources contains none to pick up implicitly. Aggravating factors found: apps/ios/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh is a live Xcode Cloud post-clone script wired to App Store Connect workflow secrets, and project.yml defines a Release archive scheme, so an App Store Connect upload pipeline exists and the ITMS-91053 rejection (enforced since May 2024, applies to TestFlight uploads too) is deterministic on first archive upload; the PebblesWidget app-extension is a second shippable bundle also lacking a manifest. Impact 3 x likelihood 4 = 12 is honest: submission-blocking but trivially fixable, plus a compliance-documentation gap for an app collecting emotional data.

findings.title: Federated (Apple/Google) signups persist NULL consent and no record binds an accepted document version
findings.detail: handle_new_user() copies terms_accepted_at/privacy_accepted_at from signup metadata and is deliberately NULL-safe because OAuth carries no consent metadata (20260729120000:10-12,24-27). The OAuth client paths send none (useSupabaseAuth.ts:159-172; SupabaseService.swift:92-138), so every Apple/Google account is created with NULL consent timestamps and nothing forces a consent step. There is also no policy-version column: profiles stores only two timestamps (20260411000001:26-27) and grep for policy_version/terms_version/privacy_version returns nothing, so even email consent records cannot identify which document version was accepted and a policy bump forces no re-acceptance. Failure scenario: a supervisory authority asks the controller to demonstrate consent (Art.7(1)) for a federated user or to show which privacy version a cohort accepted; neither can be produced. The accountability principle fails for every OAuth account and for version tracking on all accounts.
findings.evidence: 20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql:10-12,24-27; apps/web/lib/data/useSupabaseAuth.ts:159-172; apps/ios/Pebbles/Services/SupabaseService.swift:92-138; profiles cols 20260411000001_core_tables.sql:26-27; grep policy_version/terms_version -> none
findings.remediation: Capture and persist consent on the OAuth callback (write terms/privacy acceptance for federated signups) and add an accepted-document-version column bound to each timestamp, with a re-consent prompt when the version bumps; add a harness asserting non-null consent after email and each OAuth provider signup.

verification.note: Independently re-read every cited location and hunted for neutralizing guards. Migration 20260729120000 lines 11-12/24-27 confirm handle_new_user() inserts NULL consent for OAuth signups by design, and its backfill only recovers email-signup metadata. All three OAuth client paths send no consent metadata (useSupabaseAuth.ts signInWithApple/Google pass only redirectTo; iOS SupabaseService.swift 92-141; Android SupabaseService.kt signInWithGoogle, an aggravator the report did not cite). profiles has only two timestamptz columns (core_tables.sql 26-27); repo-wide grep for policy_version/terms_version/privacy_version/consent_version returns nothing, and no RPC or client code writes consent timestamps after signup, so no re-acceptance mechanism exists. No guard neutralizes the claim: on the web register page the OAuth buttons are disabled only on `submitting`, not on the consent checkboxes, and even a ticked checkbox is dropped on the OAuth path; the web login page offers OAuth with zero legal UI, so a first-time OAuth user can create an account never seeing any terms surface; iOS/Android show only a browsewrap disclaimer near the OAuth buttons, which is notice, not demonstrable consent. Failure scenario reproduced: no record can demonstrate consent for any federated account and no account records which document version was accepted. Severity 3x4 is honest; likelihood is deterministic per OAuth signup (arguably 5, so 4 is not overstated).

findings.title: The live privacy policy describes a product that does not exist and omits the sharing features that do
findings.detail: The policy (dated 2026-04-09, never updated) asserts 'We do not share your memories anywhere' while the shipped product has mutual connections, connection-visible pebbles, anonymous public share links, public profiles, and a glyph marketplace. It documents Google Gemma AI processing with a US transfer, therapist access permissions, HealthKit integration, and Cairns aggregations, none of which exist in the codebase, and omits pebble photos from the data-collected inventory. The controller contact block still contains literal '[address]' and '[telephone]' placeholders, failing Art. 13(1)(a) on its face. Users consenting at signup are consenting to a description of a different product, which undermines the validity of that consent and the Art. 13 transparency duty; the store roadmap has acknowledged the mismatch since July without a shipped fix.
findings.evidence: apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md:22, 33-34, 71, 130-176, 322-344, 409-416; sharing reality at packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260817130000_pebble_visibility_grades.sql and apps/web/app/p/[id]/page.tsx; grep -ri 'gemma|healthkit|can_view_events' over apps/web (non-docs) and packages/supabase: zero implementation hits; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-store-launch-roadmap.md:25
findings.remediation: Rewrite the policy (FR authoritative, EN courtesy) around the actual data flows: connections, visibility grades, share links, marketplace, photos, achievements; delete unshipped features or mark them future; fill controller contact details; bump the version and pair with the planned re-consent surface.

verification.note: Independently re-read the policy and re-derived every claim from the code at the audited commit. Verified: (1) en.md line 22 says "We do not share your memories anywhere" while 20260730070347_mutual_connections.sql, 20260817130000_pebble_visibility_grades.sql (RLS exposing 'private' pebbles to connections and 'public' to any authenticated user, get_shared_pebble granted to anon), apps/web/app/p/[id]/page.tsx (anonymous share links), 20260730120000_public_profiles.sql and 20260630003348_glyph_marketplace.sql all ship sharing; (2) zero implementation hits for gemma, healthkit, or can_view_general/can_view_events across all .ts/.tsx/.sql/.swift/.kt in apps/ and packages/ (docs-only), and no server-side Cairns aggregation exists (WeekRollCairn.tsx is a client-side week-header button, not the "retained indefinitely" aggregates the policy describes); (3) pebble photos exist (20260426000001_pebbles_pictures.sql; the audited commit itself ships the photo library) but the policy inventory lists only the avatar; (4) literal [address]/[telephone] placeholders at lines 33-34 and 409-410 in both EN and FR; (5) the consent path is real: register/page.tsx requires privacy_accepted linking to /docs/privacy and 20260729120000 persists privacy_accepted_at, so every signup consents to this document; (6) the roadmap spec (2026-07-28, "What blocks it") acknowledges the mismatch and the file is unchanged since 2026-04-09. Aggravating: the policy is internally contradictory (section 3.2 lists "Social sharing (if enabled)" while the preamble denies all sharing, and no section names recipients per Art. 13(1)(e)); the policy self-qualifies the data as Art. 9 health data and the product accepts minors from 13; likelihood is arguably 5 since every signup flows through the document. One nuance: the controller block does include name and email, so the Art. 13(1)(a) failure rests on the literal placeholders, not total absence of contact details. Severity 12 is honest, if anything conservative.

findings.title: No in-product reporting mechanism or in-app contact info anywhere cross-user content renders on Android
findings.detail: The Android app displays other users' content in the glyph store Commu tab (community-carved glyphs and their names via v_glyph_market) and in connections and invite previews (peer display names and glyphs), but ships zero reporting UI: no report affordance, no report string resource, and no moderation-report table exists in any migration for a report to land in. In-app developer contact information is also absent (only Terms and Privacy links exist in Settings). Play's UGC policy requires an in-product reporting mechanism for apps that surface user-generated content, and its absence is a production-review rejection risk; the decisions log itself defers reporting to a future milestone (M56), so the gap is known but unshipped. Block exists (remove-and-block on connections) and market glyphs are pre-reviewed by an admin, so two of the four pillars are present; the report and contact pillars are the failures.
findings.evidence: rg -i 'report' over apps/android/app/src/main returns no UI (only unrelated words); apps/android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml has no report/contact/support entries; features/glyph/models/GlyphMarket.kt (MarketGlyphRow over v_glyph_market) and services/ConnectionsService.kt:34-41 are the cross-user render paths; block exists at features/connections/RemoveConnectionDialog.kt:61; docs/decisions/log.md:356 'M56 adds reporting'; no report table in packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/
findings.remediation: Ship a minimal report primitive before any production Play submission: a reports table plus an insert RPC, a report action on glyph detail (GlyphDetailDrawer) and on connection rows, surfaced in the existing admin moderation queue; add a contact row (support email or link) to the Settings legal section and mirror all of it on iOS per the 1:1 rule.

verification.note: Re-verified every evidence item at the commit: no report UI or string exists anywhere under apps/android/app/src/main (only unrelated comment words); strings.xml and SettingsScreen.kt carry only Terms/Privacy links, no contact/support/feedback channel; no report table exists in any migration (only admin pre-approval of glyph submissions). Cross-user rendering confirmed: v_glyph_market (20260630003348.sql section 5) exposes other users' glyph drawings and user-entered names, rendered in GlyphsListScreen.kt:295 and GlyphDetailDrawer.kt:155; unmoderated peer display names render in ConnectionsScreen.kt:122/267 and AcceptInviteScreen.kt:155/191, the latter reachable via an anon-granted preview RPC. Block exists (RemoveConnectionDialog.kt:53-68) and market glyphs are admin pre-reviewed, as the finding said. Aggravating corroboration: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-store-launch-roadmap.md:9,25,143 lists the missing in-app report mechanism as a confirmed store compliance blocker that must be in the launch build, planned as M56 (content_reports table + report affordance + moderation contact); M56 has no spec and is unshipped while M58-era work has landed. Severity 12 is honest: impact 4 matches the repo's own launch-blocker classification; likelihood 3 correctly discounts for the app being in internal testing with M56 on the critical path before store readiness. Minor caveat, not severity-changing: the in-app contact pillar is strictly Apple 1.2 (Play requires listing-level contact info), but the primary claim about Play's in-product reporting requirement is accurate.

findings.title: No PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy ships in either iOS target while the app uses required-reason APIs
findings.detail: Neither the Pebbles app target nor the PebblesWidget extension contains a privacy manifest, and project.yml references none. The app itself uses UserDefaults through @AppStorage (a required-reason API needing an NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults declaration), and supabase-swift persists sessions on-device. Since May 2024 Apple rejects submissions whose required-reason API usage is undeclared (ITMS-91053), so the next App Store / TestFlight external submission will trip this. There is also no repo-tracked inventory of the privacy nutrition label answers, so nothing ties a future SDK or data-type addition to a declaration update. The store-launch roadmap already lists this as a v1.0 gate (M56), but at the snapshot nothing exists.
findings.evidence: find apps/ios -name '*.xcprivacy' = empty; apps/ios/project.yml:40-95 (no manifest in sources/settings); apps/ios/Pebbles/RootView.swift:25 (@AppStorage); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-store-launch-roadmap.md:25,148
findings.remediation: Add PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy to both targets declaring collected data types (account identifiers, user content, coarse usage) and NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults with reason CA92.1; commit a docs/store/ inventory mapping data types and SDKs to the label answers; add a CI presence check.

verification.note: Independently reproduced every evidence item: no .xcprivacy file exists anywhere in apps/ios (find empty); project.yml defines both targets with directory-globbed sources and no manifest; @AppStorage("hasSeenOnboarding") at Pebbles/RootView.swift:25 is a real first-party UserDefaults use (ComposerSnapshotStore.swift:9 confirms it is the app's one deliberate key), which requires an NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults/CA92.1 declaration. Hunted for neutralizers and found none: ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh only writes Secrets.xcconfig and runs xcodegen (no manifest generation), the GitHub workflows are android/arkaik/lab-note only, and I verified upstream that supabase-swift ships no PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy at all (Package.swift resources are test-target-only), so no bundled SDK manifest accidentally covers the UserDefaults category at upload validation. No repo-tracked nutrition-label inventory exists; aggravatingly, the repo's own quality framework (docs/quality/library/framework.json:1629) requires exactly the artifact that is missing, and the roadmap (2026-07-28-store-launch-roadmap.md:25,148) confirms zero code exists at the snapshot. Two immaterial errata in the finding: the fix is scheduled under M57 (Store readiness), not M56, and supabase-swift persists sessions in Keychain (not itself a required-reason API); neither weakens the claim since the app's own @AppStorage suffices to trigger ITMS-91053. Impact 3 (hard upload/submission blocker, cheap fix) and likelihood 4 (check runs at every App Store Connect upload including TestFlight since May 2024; Xcode Cloud distribution is configured and the whole M45-M57 program targets a store launch) are honest.

findings.title: No in-product reporting mechanism exists on iOS although other users' content renders in the app
findings.detail: Glyph-market listings show glyph drawings and names created by other users, and invite/connection flows show peer display names, but there is no way to report objectionable content from anywhere in the app - no report control on market items, no report flow at all, and not even a mailto fallback. Apple 1.2 requires a mechanism to report offensive content for apps with user-generated content, and the store-launch roadmap itself listed 'no in-app report/block for UGC (Apple 1.2)' as a compliance blocker; the block half has since landed (Remove and block on connections) but the report half has not. An objectionable glyph name that slips past pre-publication moderation is visible to every market visitor with no user recourse, and App Review can reject on the missing pillar.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'report' apps/ios/Pebbles/Features = zero report UI (only WobbleFlags/renderer false positives); cross-user surfaces at apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Glyph/Views/GlyphDetailDrawer.swift:46, GlyphPickerContent.swift, Connections/InviteAcceptSheet.swift:46-47; block exists at ConnectionsListView.swift:47; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-store-launch-roadmap.md:25
findings.remediation: Add a content_reports table + report_content RPC feeding the existing admin moderation surface, and a report affordance on glyph market items and connection/peer contexts on iOS (mirror on Android/web per the 1:1 rule); wire the admin queue to takedown via the existing reject/unpublish RPCs.

verification.note: Independently re-verified every evidence point at commit 1018191. (1) grep across all apps/ios Swift files: zero report UI, no mailto, no support/contact affordance in SettingsSheet; only WobbleFlags/comment false positives. (2) Cross-user UGC renders on iOS: GlyphDetailDrawer.swift shows user-entered glyph names/strokes from v_glyph_market (approved+listed submissions by any user, migrations 20260630003348 + 20260701102810); InviteAcceptSheet.swift shows peer displayName. (3) Block half landed (Remove and block in ConnectionsListView.swift, connection_blocks in 20260730070347_mutual_connections.sql) but no content_reports table exists in any migration; the M56 spec item that would add it is unlanded while M49/M50/M51 all shipped, so UGC surface area grew ahead of the report mechanism. (4) The roadmap (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-store-launch-roadmap.md) does list 'no in-app report/block for UGC (Apple 1.2)' as a store compliance blocker gating M57. Mitigations (admin pre-approval of market listings; app not yet submitted, M56 planned before M57) are already reflected in impact 3; likelihood 4 is fair since the gap is certain in the current build and only a planning doc, not code or CI, enforces fixing it before submission. Severity 12 is honest.

findings.title: Production auth and API configuration is console-only: no committed snapshot of the redirect allowlist, provider client IDs, OTP expiry, email confirmation, or SMTP settings
findings.detail: The tracked config.toml holds only local dev values (site_url and additional_redirect_urls point at 127.0.0.1, the Apple provider is disabled, Google has no section at all), while the project's own decision log makes the remote Supabase project the primary environment for all deploys. Every production auth setting therefore lives solely in the dashboard, with the only written record being scattered imperative steps inside historical plan docs with placeholder domains. Nobody can state, review, diff, or restore the production redirect allowlist or provider configuration from the repo.
