Failure scenario: a broad or wildcarded redirect URL added during debugging (or by a compromised dashboard account) goes unreviewed indefinitely and enables OAuth token interception and account takeover; alternatively, project loss or an accidental settings change cannot be restored because no authoritative record exists. The same untracked-state problem covers OTP expiry, email confirmation posture, and SMTP, so the auth hardening the schema-level controls assume cannot be verified from the repo.
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/supabase/config.toml:154-156 (local-only site_url and redirect list), :305-311 (apple disabled, no google section), :209,:217 (confirmations and OTP on defaults); docs/decisions/log.md:41-48 (remote-first deploy decision); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-26-back-office-app-design.md:170 and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-01-ios-apple-google-signin.md Task 10 (dashboard steps as the only record); grep for a production config snapshot ('site_url|redirect url|URL Configuration' across docs/) found only those prose fragments
findings.remediation: Commit a reviewed snapshot (markdown or IaC) of the production dashboard's auth, storage, and API settings (redirect allowlist, provider client IDs, OTP expiry, confirmation and SMTP posture, max_rows), treat it as the authority with dashboard changes landing as PRs to it, and add a scheduled drift check via the Supabase management API.

verification.note: Re-read all cited evidence and hunted for neutralizers; everything reproduces. config.toml:154-156 has only 127.0.0.1 redirect values, :305-311 has apple enabled=false with empty client_id and no google section at all, :209/:217 leave email confirmation off and OTP expiry at the 3600s default, and the SMTP block is commented out. The 2026-05-26 remote-first decision (docs/decisions/log.md:41-50) stands unsuperseded; no later entry, script, or workflow introduces config-as-code — the four GitHub workflows never touch Supabase config and 'supabase config push' appears nowhere. The only records of production auth settings are imperative dashboard prose with placeholders (ios-apple-google-signin plan Task 10 is explicitly '(No commit — this task is dashboard-only.)'; back-office spec step 6 uses 'admin.<consumer-domain>'). Aggravating factors found: (1) drift is already documented, not hypothetical — the 2026-04-11 apple-signin spec records the production dashboard at a 10-char symbol password policy while config.toml says 8 chars letters_digits; (2) the tracked file is production-hostile, not just incomplete — pushing it would disable Apple, leave Google unconfigured, and set the allowlist to 127.0.0.1, so it cannot serve as a restoration base; (3) shipped Google/Apple OAuth on web, iOS, and Android (android-parity-audit spec: providers 'already dashboard-configured') means every surface's login hangs off console-only state; (4) the repo's own PLT-08 rubric explicitly defines console-only prod config as a finding at maturity level 2. Impact 4 (OAuth redirect takeover surface plus unrestorable auth config for four clients) and likelihood 3 (state is certain and permanent, drift already occurred once, ad-hoc dashboard edits are institutionalized in plan docs, but the concrete attack chain remains speculative on a single-maintainer project) are honest.

findings.title: Sign-out and account deletion leave the previous user's intimate content on device and serve it to the next account
findings.detail: The composer crash-snapshot (composer-snapshot.json in the Caches directory) holds the full in-progress draft - free-text name and description, intensity/positiveness, emotion, soul and collection ids - and is cleared only on publish, server-draft save, or explicit discard, never on sign-out or account deletion. RootView's session-loss handler clears only the signed-URL cache, and the deletion path in SettingsSheet just calls signOut. Because ComposerDraftCoordinator.hydrate offers any non-empty snapshot with no user binding, the next account signing in on the same install is prompted to restore the previous user's draft verbatim. Additionally, ReferenceDataService keeps the prior user's souls and collections (names of real people in their life) in memory across sign-out, and the record flow's souls step reads that cache directly, so user B composing a pebble in the same launch sees user A's people. Handed-over and shared devices are a normal pattern for a journaling app, making this a direct cross-user exposure of special-category-adjacent content.
findings.evidence: apps/ios/Pebbles/Services/ComposerSnapshotStore.swift:29-33 (file location), 68-70 (clear only); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Path/ComposerDraftCoordinator.swift:74-105 (unconditional offerRestore); apps/ios/Pebbles/RootView.swift:161-167 (sign-out clears only snapURLs); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Profile/Sheets/SettingsSheet.swift:404-416 (deletion path); apps/ios/Pebbles/Services/ReferenceDataService.swift:22-24,41-81 (in-memory souls/collections, loaded once per launch at RootView.swift:134-135); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Record/Steps/RecordSoulsStep.swift:6,17 (reads refs.souls); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Path/Models/PebbleDraftPayload.swift:20-32 (payload fields)
findings.remediation: Add a single clear-all-local-state routine (delete the snapshot file, reset ReferenceDataService/PathStatsService/PebbleDraftsService state, remove URLCache entries) and invoke it from the RootView session-nil transition and from deleteAccount; add a Swift Testing case asserting the snapshot store and service caches are empty after the sign-out handler runs.

verification.note: Re-read every cited file plus all callers. Verified: (1) composer-snapshot.json in Caches holds the full draft (name, description, valence, emotion, soul/collection ids, snap storage paths) and its clear() is reachable only from publish, server-draft save, explicit discard, and decode failure — no auth-lifecycle caller exists anywhere (grep for removeItem/FileManager confirms). (2) RootView's session-loss handler clears only SnapURLCache; SupabaseService.signOut only calls auth.signOut; SettingsSheet.deleteAccount invokes the edge function then signOut with zero local cleanup despite its "full erasure" doc comment. (3) ComposerDraftCoordinator.hydration offers any non-empty snapshot with no user binding, so the next account is prompted to restore the prior user's draft. (4) ReferenceDataService loads souls/collections once per process from RootView's .task, is never cleared or reloaded on auth change (the service graph is built once in PebblesApp.init and RootView never leaves the hierarchy), and RecordSoulsStep/RecordCollectionStep/CreatePebbleSheet/EditPebbleSheet read the cache directly. Aggravating factors found: CreatePebbleSheet.cancelAndCleanup (lines 149-154) does not discard the snapshot, unlike the record flow's counterpart, so a plain Cancel/swipe-dismiss of the sheet composer after the 800ms debounce leaves the content on disk with no crash required; the snapshot's snap storage paths embed the prior user's user id. Minor nit not affecting severity: in a cross-launch handover the restore path filters soul/collection ids against the new user's KnownIds (PebbleDraftPayload.swift:212-215), so A's soul names render to B only in the same-launch scenario via the stale refs cache — which the finding correctly identifies as the mechanism; the intimate free-text/emotion content restores verbatim in all scenarios. Impact 4 x likelihood 3 is honest.

findings.title: Android production failures reach no one: no crash SDK, no monitored substitute, errors end at Logcat
findings.detail: The app is distributed to real users through Play internal testing on every push to main, yet has no crash reporting SDK and no documented substitute loop. Every one of the 102 error paths terminates in android.util.Log on the user's device. A crash, an auth regression, a decode failure wave after a schema change, or the record flow bricking (see the reference-data finding) would be discovered only through user complaints, if at all. Play Console vitals collect crashes automatically for Play-distributed builds, but no runbook or doc names them as watched on any cadence, and the parity audit explicitly parked the crash-reporting decision seven weeks before this snapshot. For an intimate-data product, every other reliability control on this surface currently degrades unverified.
findings.evidence: apps/android/app/build.gradle.kts:126-170 (dependency list, no reporting SDK); grep -riE 'sentry|crashlytics|bugsnag|datadog|firebase' apps/android = 0 hits; docs/android-play-deploy.md contains no vitals/monitoring section (grep -iE 'vitals|crash|monitor' = 0); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-android-parity-audit.md:138 ('Crash reporting (Play vitals vs SDK) | decision | DD, needs a decisions-log entry'); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-android-bootstrap-design.md:152 (crash reporting deferred to a future milestone).
findings.remediation: Take the parked decision: either adopt one reporting SDK (with PII scrubbing configured before first deploy, given pebble names and emotions could ride exception messages) or write the Play-vitals triage cadence into docs/android-play-deploy.md and the decision log. Fire one deliberate test crash to prove the loop closes.

verification.note: Re-verified every citation read-only. (1) apps/android/app/build.gradle.kts dependency block has no reporting SDK; repo-wide grep for sentry/crashlytics/bugsnag/datadog/firebase/acra/embrace/newrelic in apps/android = 0 hits, and no remote error sink exists in source (no logging edge-function invoke, no telemetry); 101 android.util.Log call sites across 46 files in src/main are the only error terminals (finding said 102 — immaterial). (2) .github/workflows/android-release.yml auto-publishes a signed AAB to the Play internal track on every push to main touching apps/android/**. (3) docs/android-play-deploy.md (212 lines): zero matches for vitals/crash/monitor — no watched-cadence anywhere. (4) Parity audit line confirmed verbatim ('Crash reporting (Play vitals vs SDK) | decision | DD — needs a decisions-log entry, symmetric with iOS') and docs/decisions/log.md contains no crash-reporting entry resolving it. (5) Bootstrap design defers crash reporting to 'a future Android distribution milestone'. Aggravating: that distribution milestone has effectively shipped (signing, Play Console, versioning, CI auto-publish all exist) without the crash-reporting piece, and no other surface (web/iOS/admin) has a monitoring SDK either — the two web grep hits were 'DraftsEntry' false-positives on 'sentry'. Mitigations (internal-track-only audience, passive Play vitals collection) are already priced into impact 3. Nits: gap age is ~6 weeks, not seven; Log count 101 not 102. Severity 12 (3x4) is honest.

findings.title: Production crashes and errors on iOS never reach a monitored destination
findings.detail: The iOS app has no crash-reporting or error-shipping mechanism of any kind: dependencies are Supabase, SVGView, and RiveRuntime only, and every failure path ends in an os.Logger call that lives and dies on the user's device. There is no MetricKit subscriber, no log shipping, and no documented routine for checking App Store Connect crash reports. A crash loop or a systematic decode failure in a release build would be discovered only through app-store reviews or silent churn, and every other reliability control on the surface (tri-state error UI, soft-success recovery, retry paths) degrades unverified because nobody can see whether it fires in production. For a product carrying intimate emotional data, an eventual SDK adoption must also configure PII scrubbing, which argues for doing it deliberately now rather than hastily after an incident.
findings.evidence: apps/ios/project.yml:27-36 (package list: Supabase, SVGView, RiveRuntime only); grep for 'sentry|crashlytics|bugsnag|datadog|firebase|MetricKit' across apps/ios returns zero hits; error paths terminate on-device, e.g. apps/ios/Pebbles/Services/SupabaseService.swift:61, apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Path/PathView.swift:257; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-android-parity-audit.md:138 records crash reporting as an undecided item 'symmetric with iOS'; no GitHub workflow for iOS (docs/quality/audits/2026-08/baseline.md:13).
findings.remediation: Adopt one error-reporting destination for iOS (Sentry/Crashlytics or a MetricKit-based pipeline), configure PII scrubbing before first deploy given the product's data sensitivity, wire serious handled errors (publish failure, auth failure, decode failure) in addition to crashes, write down who triages on what cadence, and fire one deliberate test error to prove the loop closes.

verification.note: Re-verified every evidence item at the snapshot commit: project.yml:27-36 lists only Supabase/SVGView/RiveRuntime; case-insensitive grep for sentry/crashlytics/bugsnag/datadog/firebase/MetricKit (plus MXMetric/appcenter/instabug/embrace) across apps/ios returns zero hits; SupabaseService.swift:61 and PathView.swift:257 both terminate in os.Logger with privacy:.private plus local view state, and no iOS code writes errors/telemetry to Supabase; parity audit line 138 confirms crash reporting is an undecided item symmetric with iOS and docs/decisions/log.md has no adoption entry; .github/workflows contains no iOS workflow, matching baseline.md:13. Tested the strongest neutralizer: Xcode Cloud is configured (apps/ios/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh), so Apple's zero-SDK crash aggregation in App Store Connect/Organizer exists as a destination — but the finding already accounts for it (no documented checking routine anywhere in the repo, verified), it covers crashes only from analytics-opted-in users, and it can never see the finding's non-crash scenario (a systematic client-side decode failure of a 200 response leaves no trace anywhere). No other surface ships errors either, so no repo pattern was diverged from. Severity 12 (3x4) is honest.

findings.title: Same-function migration re-emissions can silently drop each other's changes and no CI applies the chain or diffs re-emitted bodies; the failure already occurred once on purge_account
findings.detail: purge_account and remove_connection both grow by re-emitting the whole function body with in-body append markers. create or replace has no merge semantics and git reports no conflict, so two migrations authored in parallel off the same base silently discard each other's appends. This is not theoretical: 20260731090000 documents that 20260730070347 (connections) and 20260730090000 (achievements) each re-emitted purge_account and the later timestamp won, dropping the three connections deletes from the GDPR erasure function; the decision log records a second same-class collision on Arkaik nodes from parallel branches. The only defense today is a prose rule in CLAUDE.md, which was written after the incident. No CI job applies the migration chain to a scratch database, flags destructive DDL, or pairwise-diffs pending re-emissions of the same function name, so the next parallel-authoring collision regresses erasure or connection-severing again and ships unnoticed until a harness is manually run.
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260731090000_purge_account_union.sql:1-18 (incident record); 20260730070347_mutual_connections.sql:376 and 20260730090000_achievements.sql:266 (the colliding re-emissions); docs/decisions/log.md:433 (second collision, Arkaik nodes); .github/workflows/ contains only android.yml, android-release.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml (no db job); docs/quality/audits/2026-08/baseline.md:11 (supabase lint is a placeholder)
findings.remediation: Add a CI job on PRs touching packages/supabase/supabase/migrations that (a) applies the full chain to a scratch Postgres (supabase db reset against a service container), (b) fails when two pending migrations re-emit the same function name without a union marker, and (c) greps new files for destructive DDL keywords requiring a sign-off label. Add 'rollback path' as a required line in the migration PR checklist.

verification.note: Re-checked every citation. (1) Incident record: /home/user/pbbls/packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260731090000_purge_account_union.sql lines 1-18 state exactly the claimed failure: 20260730070347 (connections) and 20260730090000 (achievements) were authored in parallel off 20260729213348, each re-emitted purge_account with only its own section-(4) append, the achievements copy won by timestamp, and the merged history silently dropped the three connections deletes from the GDPR erasure function. (2) Both colliding re-emissions verified in the migration files (mutual_connections ~line 376, achievements ~line 266); purge_account is re-emitted whole in 5 separate migrations. (3) remove_connection carries the same in-body append marker (mutual_connections line 320-324: 'M52/M53: sever seams and pairs HERE... This is the purge_account append-marker pattern'), so future re-emission of that function is scheduled work, not hypothetical. (4) Second same-class collision confirmed in docs/decisions/log.md (#725 entry, ~line 433): two parallel branches re-emitted the same three Arkaik nodes and 'collided exactly the way the standing create or replace rule warns about'. (5) No mechanical guard exists: .github/workflows contains only android.yml, android-release.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml with zero references to supabase/migrations/db; no git hooks or husky; supabase lint is literally 'echo placeholder' (package.json, matching baseline.md line 11); turbo.json defines no test task that could run the harnesses; verify-account-purge.ts is a manual script. (6) Timeline claim verified via git: the CLAUDE.md prose rule landed 2026-08-02 (#694), after the 2026-07-31 union fix (#689). Mitigations found and weighed: the first incident never reached a live database (caught pre-push, union file lines 16-17) and the Arkaik collision was caught at merge, but both catches were exactly the manual vigilance the finding says is the only defense. Aggravating: both marked functions are designed to keep growing by whole-body re-emission, and parallel-branch authoring is routine in this repo (multiple decision-log entries document concurrently open branches), so exposure recurs by design. Impact 4 (silent regression of GDPR erasure or connection severing reaching the linked project until a harness is manually run) and likelihood 3 (two occurrences in under a month, prose-only defense) are honest.

findings.title: delete_pebble strands the pebble's photos in storage on every surface; no cleanup path exists before full account deletion
findings.detail: delete_pebble deletes the pebbles row and lets snaps rows cascade, but never returns the snaps' storage_path values and no server-side job removes the objects. All three clients call the RPC directly with no storage cleanup, so deleting a pebble that carries photos leaves {user_id}/{snap_id}/original.jpg and thumb.jpg in the pebbles-media bucket indefinitely. The single-snap removal flow proves the team knows the pattern (delete_pebble_media returns the path so the client can sweep, and web does), but the whole-pebble flow skips it. In an intimate-records product the user's expectation is that deleting the moment deletes its photo; instead the bytes persist, invisible to every surface, until the terminal delete-account sweep. This is exactly the criterion's 'file-plus-row pairs have a defined consistency story' clause failing for the highest-frequency deletion flow, and it also accrues storage cost and data-minimization exposure.
findings.evidence: delete_pebble body: packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260411000003_rpc_functions.sql:351-379 (re-emitted unchanged in shape at 20260411000005_security_hardening.sql:361); contrast delete_pebble_media returning storage_path at 20260426000002_pebble_media_edit.sql:234-249 with web cleanup at apps/web/lib/data/supabase-provider.ts:541-551; delete_pebble called with no storage cleanup at apps/web/lib/data/supabase-provider.ts:773, apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Path/PathView.swift:267, apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/pbbls/android/services/PebbleWriteService.kt:110; only sweep is account deletion, supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts:69-92
findings.remediation: Extend delete_pebble to return the deleted snaps' storage_path array (keeping create/update/delete sibling symmetry) and have each client sweep the returned paths like the delete_pebble_media flow already does; or add a scheduled orphan sweep that lists pebbles-media prefixes and removes objects whose snap_id no longer exists in snaps. Extend verify-account-purge or a new harness to assert zero orphaned objects after a pebble deletion.

verification.note: Re-read every cited location: delete_pebble (20260411000003_rpc_functions.sql:351-379, search_path-pinned re-emission at 20260411000005:361-389) deletes the pebbles row and cascades snaps without returning storage_path or touching storage.objects; no later migration, trigger, cron, edge function, or admin tool sweeps pebbles-media (only functions: backfill-pebble-render, compose-pebble, compose-pebble-update, delete-account; the sole prefix purge is delete-account/index.ts:69-92). All client call sites are bare RPC calls with no storage cleanup: web supabase-provider.ts:772-776, Android PebbleWriteService.kt:107-117, and iOS has THREE such entry points (PathView.swift:267 plus uncited SoulDetailView.swift:185 and CollectionDetailView.swift:186). The contrast holds: delete_pebble_media returns storage_path and web/iOS sweep the two files after it (supabase-provider.ts:537-555). Aggravating: the gap is documented, deliberate, unpaid debt since April 2026 — specs 2026-04-26-ios-pebbles-pictures-design.md:39,64 ('Orphan files accepted in V1... handled by the V2 sweep') and 2026-04-27-ios-pebble-deletion-design.md:72 ('Storage cleanup is out of scope... a follow-up issue should track storage hygiene'), with the follow-up issue drafted in the plan (2026-04-26-ios-pebbles-pictures.md:2218) but no sweep ever landed; a deferred IOU is neither fail-safe ordering nor orphan cleanup, so the REL-03 clause fails as stated. Mitigating but score-neutral: the bucket is private (public=false) with owner-scoped RLS, so orphans are never cross-user visible and per-file size is capped at 1.5MB — which is exactly why impact 3 (not higher) is right, while likelihood 4 is honest since every photo-carrying pebble deletion on any surface orphans deterministically.

findings.title: Failed store load renders the first-run empty state on /path and other core screens; DataProvider's error and refreshStore are consumed by zero components
findings.detail: DataProvider catches any loadFromSupabase failure, sets the store to EMPTY_STORE with loading=false, and exposes error and refreshStore through context. No component in the codebase reads either: all 30 useDataProvider() destructures take only provider/store/setStore/loading. On a transient network failure at app open (flaky mobile connection, Supabase blip, any one of the 9 parallel queries failing), /path renders the week roll with zero pebbles and WeekPath falls through to PathEmptyState, the record-your-first-pebble CTA. A user with years of entries is shown a first-run screen claiming their life record is empty, with no error message and no retry; the same conflation hits souls, collections and wallet (WalletView renders the 'empty' string whenever history is [] and loading is false, ignoring the error member useWallet exposes). The Supabase SW rule is NetworkOnly, so no cached response softens this. The catch block also logs nothing, violating the repo's own error-visibility rule in docs/agents/data-and-async.md.
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/layout/DataProvider.tsx:33-40,67; grep 'const {...} = useDataProvider()' across apps/web shows no destructure of error or refreshStore; apps/web/app/path/page.tsx:8-13; apps/web/components/path/PathScreen.tsx:85-92; apps/web/components/path/WeekPath.tsx:48; apps/web/components/wallet/WalletView.tsx:37-38; apps/web/app/sw.ts:20-26
findings.remediation: In the shell that hosts store-backed screens (or per screen), branch on the already-exposed error: render a distinct failure state with a retry button wired to the already-exposed refreshStore, and add a labeled console.error in DataProvider's catch. Both hooks already exist unused, so this is a rendering change only.

verification.note: Re-read every cited file at the exact lines. DataProvider.tsx:33-40 swallows any loadFromSupabase failure into EMPTY_STORE with loading=false and no console logging (violating docs/agents/data-and-async.md's error-visibility rule, line 20). Greps independently confirm all 30 useDataProvider() destructures take only provider/store/setStore/loading and no other code touches DataContext, so error and refreshStore have zero consumers. The /path chain holds: buildWeekRollEntries always seeds the current week, so an empty store renders WeekPath's PathEmptyState ('Carve a pebble' CTA) with all historical weeks silently gone; WalletView.tsx:37-38 renders the 'empty' string while ignoring the error member useWallet exposes; sw.ts:20-26 is NetworkOnly for *.supabase.co. Aggravating factors found: (1) after a failure activeUserIdRef stays set, so the guard at DataProvider.tsx:57 blocks every future reload for the page lifetime and there is no online/visibilitychange recovery, meaning only a hard page reload recovers; (2) setProvider(null) makes every mutation hook throw 'Not authenticated' at a signed-in user who follows the CTA into the record flow; (3) app/error.tsx can never fire because the error is swallowed. Two minor precision nits that do not move severity: only 6 of the 9 parallel queries throw on error (collectionPebbles/karma/bounce silently degrade), and the empty-state copy is week-scoped ('Fresh week') rather than a literal first-run message, though the collapsed week roll gives the same your-data-is-gone impression. Impact 3 x likelihood 4 is honest for a mobile-first PWA whose home screen does this on any single failed core query at cold open.

findings.title: No production error reporting on the web client: every failure terminates at the user's device console
findings.detail: The web app has no crash/error SDK, no log shipping, and no alerting. All ~70 labeled console.error/console.warn sites (publish failures, store-load failures, signing failures, soft-success warnings) emit to the browser console of the affected user and reach no human. Combined with the REL-01 fake-empty behavior, a production regression in the load path would surface only as users silently seeing empty screens; the maintainer would learn of it from complaints or never. Edge-function and server-route errors do land in Supabase/Vercel logs, but no alert rule or documented triage cadence exists anywhere in the repo, so those dashboards are watched by nobody as far as the repository can demonstrate. For an intimate-data product whose grading profile weights trust heavily, unobserved production failure is a standing reliability hazard.
findings.evidence: apps/web/package.json:14-60 (no reporting SDK); grep -rn 'sentry|bugsnag|crashlytics|datadog|logrocket|analytics' over apps/web/package.json, apps/admin/package.json, package.json returns nothing; .github/workflows/ contains no monitoring or web workflow; docs/decisions/log.md grep for monitoring/crash/observability returns nothing; sample terminal sites apps/web/lib/data/supabase-provider.ts:171,761 and apps/web/components/record/flow/RecordFlow.tsx:301
findings.remediation: Add an error-reporting SDK (e.g. Sentry) to the web client and edge functions with beforeSend scrubbing configured for this product's sensitivity (strip pebble names/descriptions, emails, storage paths), disable default PII capture, wire the existing labeled catch paths to it, and document who triages on what cadence. Verify the pipeline with a deliberate test error.

verification.note: Re-checked every evidence item read-only at the cited commit. (1) apps/web/package.json (read in full): no error-reporting SDK; only sonner (user-facing toasts). (2) Repo-wide grep for sentry/bugsnag/crashlytics/datadog/logrocket/rollbar/posthog/etc.: every hit is a false positive (SVG "highlight" shape names, admin analytics UI components, and the quality-criteria docs themselves). (3) Counted 75 console.error/console.warn occurrences across 39 files in apps/web, matching the "~70 sites" claim; verified the three cited sites verbatim: supabase-provider.ts:171 (signed-URL failure warn), supabase-provider.ts:755-767 (soft-success warn plus edge-fn failure console.error), RecordFlow.tsx:301 (publish failure console.error). (4) The global Next.js error boundary apps/web/app/error.tsx also terminates at console.error(error) with no shipping, so even unhandled render crashes reach no one. (5) .github/workflows contains only android.yml, android-release.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml; no monitoring or web workflow. (6) docs/decisions/log.md has no monitoring/observability/alerting entry; no log drain, alert rule, health check, uptime monitor, or triage doc exists anywhere (all "triage" hits are the unrelated task-size triage in CLAUDE.md/README); apps/web/vercel.json is schema-only. (7) The admin "logs" surface is the Lab changelog (LogForm/CoverImageInput), not error observability, and no edge function persists errors to a table. (8) Spot-checked the REL-01 interaction: useDomains.ts:92-94 catches a load failure, console.errors, and just sets loading=false with no error state, so the screen renders as empty. Aggravating factor: docs/agents/data-and-async.md ("Error visibility & logging") codifies console.warn/console.error as the required terminal handling for every failable async path, so the console-only pattern is the project's institutionalized standard and new code will perpetuate it. Severity is honest: impact 3 equals the REL-08 criterion's own default (which explicitly states device-console logging "is recognized as reaching no one"), and likelihood 4 fairly reflects a standing structural gap while conceding the undemonstrable possibility of manual dashboard-watching.

findings.title: No age gate exists at Android signup while the terms promise a 13+ minimum and French parental-consent machinery that is not implemented
findings.detail: The terms require users to be 13+ and require parental consent for ages 13-15 in France (where the Art. 8 digital consent age is 15, as the policy itself acknowledges); the policy details parental rights over minors' data. None of it is implemented: Android signup collects no birthdate or attestation on either the email or the Google path, nothing is recorded server-side, and no parental-consent flow exists on any surface. An intimate emotional journal with social features (connections, public profiles, a marketplace) admitting 13-year-olds without the legally required consent mechanics is simultaneously an Art. 8 defect and Play target-audience exposure, and the unimplemented promises in the controller's own documents aggravate rather than mitigate it. No store age-rating or target-audience metadata is committed to the repo to verify declarations against.
findings.evidence: apps/web/docs/terms/en.md:87 (13+ and parental consent 13-15); apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md:278-297 (France 15, accepting from 13, parental rights); grep -rin 'birth|dob|age' over apps/android auth/onboarding modules and res/values*/strings.xml returns no age UI; packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql:14-31 (trigger stores nothing age-related); docs/android-play-deploy.md (no content-rating or Data-safety step)
findings.remediation: Add a birthdate or over-threshold attestation step to signup on every path, record it server-side with the consent evidence, refuse under-15 in France (or implement the promised parental-consent flow), and commit the Play target-audience/content-rating answers to the repo so drift is reviewable.

verification.note: Independently re-read every cited artifact. Terms §3.1 (13+ min, France 13-15 parental consent) and privacy §10 (France 15, accepting from 13, parental rights) verified verbatim. Android AuthScreen.kt has only two terms/privacy acceptance checkboxes and no age or birthdate UI anywhere in apps/android; SupabaseService.signUp sends only terms/privacy timestamps and signInWithGoogle sends no metadata at all; the handle_new_user trigger (20260729120000 migration) stores nothing age-related and its own comment confirms OAuth signups carry no consent metadata whatsoever; database.ts has no age/birthdate column in any table; grep across web and iOS surfaces confirms no parental-consent flow exists anywhere; android-play-deploy.md covers internal testing only and explicitly defers the content-rating/data-safety form. Aggravating factors found: privacy §10.2 affirmatively asserts 'We ask you to confirm this consent during sign-up' (a concrete false statement, not just an unimplemented promise); terms (13-15) and privacy (13-14) contradict each other on the parental-consent band; and the Google OAuth signup class records zero consent proof of any kind. Downgrade attempt (Android is internal-testing-only) fails: the Art. 8 defect is structural on all signups, the identical gap ships on the production web PWA, and likelihood 3 already prices in current distribution. Severity 12 (4x3) is honest.

findings.title: A stolen Android session can purge the account, rotate the password, and widen exposure with no re-authentication anywhere
findings.detail: Every high-harm action on the surface gates only on a live session: the delete-account edge function authenticates the JWT and immediately purges (the only confirmation is a client-side dialog); the public-profile flip and per-pebble visibility widening to 'public' are plain authenticated RPC calls; and password change goes through auth.updateUser with secure_password_change = false in the committed auth config, so a hot session can set a new password without knowing the current one - locking the real owner out - with email confirmations disabled and no security-notification evidence. There is no global sign-out entry point (signOut uses the library default local scope). For a product holding emotional histories, photos and named third parties, an unlocked handset or hijacked session therefore has no ceiling short of total, irreversible destruction or exposure of the account.
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts:51-57 (JWT-only precondition); apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/pbbls/android/features/profile/SettingsScreen.kt:194-207,588-599 (client-side confirm only), :171-173 (setPublicProfile on session alone); services/ProfileService.kt:78-81 (updateUser password); packages/supabase/supabase/config.toml:211 (secure_password_change = false), :209 (email confirmations off); SupabaseService.kt:196-202 (local-scope signOut, no global revocation)
findings.remediation: Require a server-verified fresh credential (password re-entry or fresh OAuth) before purge, password/email change, and public-profile enable; enable secure_password_change and security-notification emails in the auth config; add a global sign-out entry; freeze with a stale-session harness attempt against each RPC.

verification.note: Independently re-read every cited location. delete-account/index.ts:50-66 gates the full purge on auth.getUser() alone (admin client runs purge_account immediately; the function is idempotent/resumable so partial failures converge to total deletion); SettingsScreen.kt:194-207 calls it behind only a tap-to-confirm AlertDialog (DeleteDialogs.kt, no typed phrase/password/biometric, and no app lock exists anywhere in apps/android); ProfileService.kt:78-82 rotates the password via auth.updateUser with config.toml:211 secure_password_change=false, :209 enable_confirmations=false, and the password_changed notification template commented out (:234-238); setPublicProfile (ProfileService.kt:106-113) and update_pebble's visibility coalesce (20260729140000:335) widen exposure on session alone; SupabaseService.kt:196-202 uses supabase-kt's default local-scope signOut and SignOutScope appears nowhere in the repo. A repo-wide grep for reauth/step-up/nonce/current-password hits only the SAF-07 criterion docs themselves. Aggravating: RLS makes 'public' pebbles readable by every authenticated user and get_shared_pebble is granted to anon, so widening reaches anonymous readers by link. Mitigations considered and rejected as downgrades: password lockout is owner-recoverable via email reset (double_confirm_changes=true blocks silent email change), and config.toml is local-dev config, but hosted Supabase defaults secure password change off too and the irreversible-purge harm is independent of the password point. Severity 12 (4x3) is honest.

findings.title: iOS ships zero crisis resources and celebrates maximum-negative entries identically to positive ones
findings.detail: An emotion journal is disproportionately likely to be open at the moment a user is in crisis, and the iOS app has no support pathway anywhere: no resources screen, no helpline string, no locale-aware crisis key in the string catalog. Worse, the completion path is valence-blind: publishing a maximum-intensity 'devastated' entry fires the same celebration haptic and ceramic sound, renders a sparkle with '+N karma', and can stack a trophy 'Achievement unlocked' card (for example the first-time-recording-this-emotion badge) directly over the user's worst moment. This is the exact l0 configuration the criterion describes, and the same gap exists on the other clients, so there is no pattern to copy.
findings.evidence: grep -ril 'crisis|helpline|suicide|self-harm' apps/ios returns nothing; apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Record/RecordFlowView.swift:250-260 (publish fires karma.notifyEarned and achievements.fireCheck with no valence branch); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Record/Steps/RecordSuccessStep.swift:43-53; apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Karma/KarmaNotificationService.swift:41-53; apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Karma/AchievementMomentView.swift:34-60
findings.remediation: Add a bundled, localized crisis-resources screen (per-locale numbers: 988 for en-US contexts, 3114 for France, plus findahelpline-style links), reachable within one tap of the success step. Branch the completion path on high-negative valence plus high intensity: suppress the sound, haptic, karma line, and achievement queue, and show a calm acknowledgment with the support affordance. Pin the branch with a unit test on the step logic.

verification.note: Independently re-verified every evidence item at the cited paths. (1) Crisis absence: grep for crisis/helpline/suicide/self-harm/hotline across apps/ios yields only binary font and SVG path-data coincidences; Localizable.xcstrings has zero crisis keys; the only repo-wide self-harm mention is a prohibited-conduct clause in the web terms, and android/admin/packages have nothing, confirming no cross-surface pattern to copy. (2) Valence-blind celebration: RecordFlowView.swift publish() (lines 250-263) unconditionally fires karma.notifyEarned and achievements.fireCheck with no valence branch, and the server guarantees the celebration triggers: compute_karma_delta (20260411000005_security_hardening.sql) takes no valence input and starts at delta := 1, so karmaDelta >= 1 for every published pebble, meaning the amount > 0 guard in KarmaNotificationService (line 43) always passes and haptic + ceramic sound fire (lines 47-49) identically for maximum-negative entries; RecordSuccessStep renders the sparkle +N karma whenever karma > 0 (always). (3) Trophy stacking: the achievements catalog migration (20260730090000_achievements.sql:108-130) auto-generates an emotion-first badge for every emotion including sadness, anxiety, shame, guilt, and hopeless, and AchievementMomentView is hosted by the overlay window that floats above whatever fired it, so an Achievement unlocked trophy card lands directly over the success step. Aggravating factor: because emotion_first badges are per-emotion, the trophy-over-worst-moment configuration is guaranteed for every user the first time they record each negative emotion, a designed-in first-run experience rather than an edge case. One minor imprecision that does not affect severity: 'devastated' is not an actual seeded slug (the extremes are hopeless/sadness/anxiety at lowlight-large valence); the finding used it illustratively. Impact 4 x likelihood 3 = 12 is honest.

findings.title: No age gate exists at signup despite the terms declaring 13+ and promising a parental-consent confirmation
findings.detail: The published terms require users to be at least 13 and the privacy policy states that 13-14 year olds must have parental consent which 'we ask you to confirm during sign-up'. Nothing in the iOS signup implements any of this: no date-of-birth field, no attestation checkbox, no parental-consent step, and nothing recorded server-side. OAuth signups collect even less. France's Art. 8 implementation sets the digital consent age at 15, so admitting 13-14 year olds on a self-declared basis with an unimplemented parental-consent promise is a consent-validity defect for exactly the cohort the policy claims to protect, in an app that records emotional states. Store metadata (age rating, target audience) is not committed anywhere in the repo, so declared-versus-enforced drift cannot even be checked.
findings.evidence: apps/web/docs/terms/en.md:87 (13+ minimum, parental consent 13-15); apps/web/docs/privacy/en.md:276-296 (section 10, 'We ask you to confirm this consent during sign-up'); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Auth/AuthView.swift:37-118 (email, password, two document checkboxes only); grep -rin 'birth|dob|minor|parental' apps/ios/Pebbles returns no relevant hit; packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260729120000_handle_new_user_consent.sql:14-31 (trigger stores no age or attestation)
findings.remediation: Add a birthdate or over-threshold attestation step to signup on all clients, persist it via the signup trigger, refuse under-13, and implement the promised parental-consent confirmation for 13-14 (or raise the floor to 15 for France and simplify). Commit the store age-rating declarations to the repo alongside the enforced minimum.

verification.note: Independently re-read every cited file. Terms en.md:87 sets 13+ with parental consent for French 13-15s; privacy en.md section 10 (and the French fr.md:254-271 identically) promises 'We ask you to confirm this consent during sign-up.' AuthView.swift collects only email, password, and two document checkboxes (canSubmit at lines 170-191 gates on nothing else); SupabaseService.signUp sends only terms_accepted_at/privacy_accepted_at, and the 20260729120000 migration stores only those two timestamps with no age or parental-attestation column anywhere in the schema. The migration's own comment confirms OAuth signups carry no consent metadata at all. Fresh greps across apps/ios, apps/web, apps/android, and packages/supabase for birth/dob/minor/parental/age-gate patterns returned only false positives, and the web register page (apps/web/app/register/page.tsx) has no age handling either, so no surface or server-side guard neutralizes the claim. No fastlane/store metadata or age-rating keys exist in the repo (project.yml has none), confirming drift is uncheckable. Aggravating: the policy declares Art. 9(2)(a) explicit consent for sensitive emotional data, and the sign-up-confirmation promise is an affirmative false statement in both languages. Severity 12 (impact 4, likelihood 3) is honest for a structural consent-validity defect present on every minor signup path.

findings.title: Karma and achievements are conditioned on emotional disclosure: per-emotion first-record badges and disclosure-volume karma, celebrated on iOS
findings.detail: compute_karma_delta pays more karma the more the user discloses about a moment: +1 for writing a description, +1 per reflective card up to 4, +1 for naming a person, +1 for attaching a photo. The emotion_first achievement family mints one badge (with karma reward) per seeded emotion for the first pebble carrying it, including negative emotions such as 'discouraged', 'disgusted', 'drained', turning the emotion catalog into a collect-them-all mechanic over mental states. iOS renders both: '+N karma' with a sparkle on the success step and a trophy card at unlock. Deleting a pebble claws back its karma, potentially into negative debt, so retaining earned karma requires retaining the disclosure. No written boundary decouples rewards from emotional content anywhere in the repo. This is the pattern EDPB deceptive-design guidance and the criterion's l0/l1 anchors describe: rewards pressuring disclosure of sensitive content.
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260411000003_rpc_functions.sql:5-45 (compute_karma_delta disclosure scoring) and 370-374 (deletion clawback); packages/supabase/supabase/migrations/20260730090000_achievements.sql:108-117 (per-emotion achievement generation) and 219-221 (emotion_first grant condition reads p.emotion_id); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Record/Steps/RecordSuccessStep.swift:43-53; apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Karma/AchievementMomentView.swift:34-60; docs/decisions/log.md:90-91 (negative-debt design)
findings.remediation: Re-key rewards to neutral activity (a flat per-pebble grant), retire or neutralize the emotion_first family (sync_achievement_catalog makes this a data change), stop clawing back karma on deletion of the user's own entries, and write the decoupling rule into the standing cross-surface rules with a migration-grep signal that fails when a grant condition references emotion columns.

verification.note: Independently re-read every cited location plus surrounding wiring. Confirmed: compute_karma_delta (20260411000003_rpc_functions.sql:16-45) pays karma monotonically with disclosure volume (description, up to 4 cards, souls, domains, glyph, snaps, cap 10); delete_pebble (lines 365-377) reverses the full earned karma and docs/decisions/log.md (2026-06-29 wallet entry) deliberately allows the balance to go negative, so keeping karma requires keeping the disclosure; sync_achievement_catalog generates one emotion_first badge per row of public.emotions (38 emotions incl. hopeless, lonely, ashamed, guilty, discouraged, disgusted, drained), pebbles.emotion_id is NOT NULL so every moment must carry an emotion, and check_achievements grants on a direct read of p.emotion_id; iOS celebrates both (RecordSuccessStep +N karma sparkle; RecordFlowView:259 fires achievements.fireCheck() on record success, so the AchievementMomentView trophy fires right after the disclosing act); grep of docs/ finds no written boundary decoupling rewards from emotional content outside the audit framework itself, matching the criterion's l1 anchor. One detail is overstated but not load-bearing: seeded/generated emotion_first badges carry karma_reward = 0 (default, never set nonzero anywhere; the paid CTE filters karma_reward > 0 and the iOS karma line is hidden at 0), so as shipped they mint a celebrated badge but no karma; only the later admin RPC could attach one. Aggravating factors found: update_pebble (lines 333-342) also claws back karma when disclosure is edited out, so even redacting a description forfeits karma without deleting the pebble; badges are permanent and write-locked with no revocation path; the check also retro-grants on every achievements screen open. Impact 3 and likelihood 4 are honest: the mechanics fire unconditionally for every user on every pebble, while harm is wellbeing/dark-pattern pressure and regulatory-guidance exposure rather than a data leak.

findings.title: Account purge, public-profile flip, and visibility widening gate only on a valid session, not recent re-authentication
findings.detail: For a product holding emotional histories, photos, and named third parties, a stolen or hot session can irreversibly destroy or publicly expose the account with no elevation. purge_account is invoked by the delete-account edge function on the forwarded JWT alone (functions/delete-account/index.ts:50-63) and the RPC has no recent-auth precondition (20260729201326:40-53). Making a profile public and claiming a handle, and widening a pebble to 'public', are plain owner-scoped client updates with no server-verified confirmation (20260730120000:118-120; update_pebble via visibility). config sets secure_password_change=false (config.toml:211), so a hot session can also rotate the password without the old one. Failure scenario: an attacker with a live session token (shared device, XSS, stolen cookie) silently purges the victim's entire journal or flips every secret pebble to public, with no re-auth challenge and no security notification, and the exposure is irreversible.
findings.evidence: functions/delete-account/index.ts:50-63; 20260729201326_account_deletion_purge.sql:40-53; supabase/config.toml:211 (secure_password_change=false); 20260730120000_public_profiles.sql:118-120
findings.remediation: Require recent re-authentication or a server-verified confirmation (e.g. a short-lived reauth nonce checked in the RPC/edge function) for account purge, public-profile enablement, and bulk visibility widening; enable secure_password_change and security-notification email templates so credential changes revoke sessions and notify the user.

verification.note: Independently re-read every cited location plus surrounding guards. delete-account edge function (index.ts:50-63) gates solely on auth.getUser() over the forwarded JWT, then uses the service-role client to run purge_account, wipe the storage prefix, and auth.admin.deleteUser — no re-auth, no server-verified confirmation, no grace period, no notification. purge_account (20260729201326:40-53) checks only p_user_id non-null; its service-role lock is bypassed by design via the edge function. config.toml:211 has secure_password_change=false (also the Supabase default) with the password-changed notification template commented out and MFA (TOTP/phone) fully disabled; grep finds zero AAL/MFA/re-auth checks anywhere in the package. public_profiles migration lines 118-120 state verbatim the public_profile toggle is a direct client update, and set_handle is security-invoker owner-RLS only. Pebble widening confirmed via 20260817130000: owner-scoped write flips visibility to 'public', after which pebbles_select RLS exposes the row to every authenticated user and get_shared_pebble to anon by uuid. Client delete flow (DeleteAccountSection.tsx) is a UI-only dialog. Aggravating: web PWA stores the Supabase session incl. refresh token in localStorage (direct XSS-to-hot-session path); no soft-delete window; silent password rotation enables lockout before purge. Minor caveats that do not move the score: config.toml is the committed local-dev config (hosted setting is dashboard-managed, but false is the platform default), and the visibility/profile flips are revocable unlike the purge. Severity 4x3=12 is honest.

findings.title: Recording a maximum-negative emotional state yields a karma reward and no crisis pathway anywhere on the surface
findings.detail: The product's core interaction invites users to record distress, yet the web surface contains zero crisis resources: no helpline strings in either locale, no support page in the docs manifest, and nothing reachable from the recording flow. Worse, the completion screen is identical for every valence: after recording a maximum-negative, maximum-intensity moment the user is shown a Sparkle icon and '+N karma', a gamified celebration of the disclosure. A user recording self-harm-adjacent distress receives a reward animation and no support affordance, which is the exact anti-pattern the criterion exists to prevent. The framework checklist marks zero crisis-string hits on a client as an automatic finding.
findings.evidence: grep -ril 'crisis|helpline|suicide' apps/web: only docs/terms/en.md:157 (a conduct prohibition); apps/web/docs/index.json (no support page); apps/web/components/record/flow/steps/RecordSuccessStep.tsx:40-45 (unconditional karma sparkle); no valence branch in components/record/flow/RecordFlow.tsx
findings.remediation: Add a localized (EN/FR, country-correct numbers) resources surface bundled in the PWA precache; branch the success step on high-negative valence to suppress the karma celebration and show a quiet supportive affordance within one tap; pin the branch with a component test.

verification.note: Independently re-verified every claim. (1) Crisis strings: a wider grep than the auditor's (adding hotline, 988, 3114, 'need help', 'santé mentale') over apps/web finds only the conduct prohibition in docs/terms/en.md:157 and fr.md:153; the i18n files lib/i18n/messages/{en,fr}.json have zero support copy; the app/ route tree has no help/support route; docs/index.json holds only four legal pages. (2) The reward is not merely unconditional but structurally guaranteed: RecordSuccessStep.tsx:40-45 gates the Sparkle + '+N karma' line on karmaDelta > 0, and computeKarmaDelta (lib/data/karma.ts, mirroring the SQL RPC) awards +1 base for every pebble regardless of valence, so usePebbles.ts always fires onKarmaEarned with delta >= 1 on publish — the guard never suppresses the celebration. (3) Full read of RecordFlow.tsx confirms no valence branch; draft.valence only enters the payload, and the success copy is identical in both locales. Aggravating factors found: the emotional disclosure is mandatory (canPublish requires emotionId, and the catalog includes Fear, Sadness, Shame); the alternate single-screen composer path is equally celebratory (notifyKarma pill fires when the callback is omitted, usePebbles.ts:29); and fireAchievementCheck runs after every publish, so an achievement toast can stack a second gamified celebration on a distress entry. Impact 4 x likelihood 3 is honest — the anti-pattern fires deterministically on every negative recording and the missing crisis pathway is a whole-surface absence.

findings.title: A stolen session can purge the account, change the password, and widen visibility with no re-authentication anywhere
findings.detail: Every high-harm action on web is gated only by possession of a live session cookie. Account deletion shows a client-side dialog and the delete-account edge function requires nothing beyond a valid JWT before running the irreversible purge. Password change calls auth.updateUser with no current-password check and the committed auth config sets secure_password_change = false. Flipping a profile public and widening a pebble's visibility to public are plain session-authenticated writes. No security-notification emails are configured (confirmations disabled, SMTP commented out), so a takeover is silent, and no password-reset flow exists for the victim to recover with. For an intimate-data product this means one XSS, one shared device, or one stolen cookie reaches unrecoverable destruction or exposure of the account's entire contents with zero friction.
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts:50-56 (JWT-only); apps/web/components/settings/DeleteAccountSection.tsx:43-54 (client dialog); apps/web/lib/data/useSupabaseAuth.ts:233-238; packages/supabase/supabase/config.toml:209,211,224-230 (enable_confirmations=false, secure_password_change=false, no SMTP); apps/web/app/settings/page.tsx:117 (public flip); grep resetPasswordForEmail over apps/web: zero
findings.remediation: Require recent re-authentication (password or OAuth re-prompt) server-side before purge, password change, and profile-public/visibility-widening writes; enable secure_password_change and confirmation/notification emails with real SMTP; add a password-reset flow; revoke other sessions on credential change.

verification.note: Independently re-read every cited file plus surrounding guards. delete-account (index.ts:50-63) is gated solely by auth.getUser() on the forwarded JWT, then runs purge_account, storage wipe, and auth.admin.deleteUser with no password re-entry, confirmation token, or grace period; the web UI (DeleteAccountSection.tsx:43-54) is a plain AlertDialog. updatePassword (useSupabaseAuth.ts:233-238) calls auth.updateUser({password}) with no current-password check, and grep confirms zero reauthenticate/nonce/resetPasswordForEmail handling anywhere in apps/web (the reported grep hits are French-locale false positives), so the app is structurally built for secure_password_change=false. config.toml:209/211 and the commented SMTP and password-changed-notification blocks check out as written; caveat, this file governs only the local stack (no `supabase config push` in scripts or CI), but hosted GoTrue defaults match these values and the clients carry no reauth code, so the inference to production holds. settings/page.tsx:117 flips public_profile via a plain RLS update, and migration 20260817130000 confirms a pebble widened to 'public' is readable by all authenticated users and anonymously by uuid via security-definer get_shared_pebble. No password reset or recovery flow exists on any surface (web, iOS, Android, admin), so an email-auth victim is unrecoverable after an attacker password change. Aggravating factors found: session tokens are in JS-readable cookies (createBrowserClient from @supabase/ssr), MFA is fully disabled, [auth.sessions] timebox/inactivity timeout are commented out so shared-device sessions persist indefinitely, and Android's ProfileService.kt:79 repeats the no-reauth password change, showing this is the deliberate cross-surface pattern. Impact 4 x likelihood 3 is honestly calibrated: irreversible purge or intimate-data exposure once any session is compromised, with the session-compromise precondition keeping likelihood at 3.

findings.title: Cross-user denial is proven for only 3 of ~30 application tables and a handful of RPCs, with no completeness check and no CI run
findings.detail: The denial tests that exist (pebble_drafts full CRUD denial, pebbles read/write matrix, anon projections) are excellent, but coverage is a hand-maintained subset: souls, collections, glyphs, snaps, karma_events, wallet_balances, bounces, the glyph marketplace tables, the connections trio, achievement_unlocks, logs, log_reactions, and direct profiles selects have no automated cross-user or anon denial assertion anywhere; definer RPCs update_pebble, delete_pebble, remove_connection, spend_karma, and every admin_* function (as a non-admin caller) have no refusal test. Nothing diffs the covered list against the schema, so a new table or RPC ships with zero denial proof and no visible gap. The suite also only runs when a human remembers to run it against the remote project. On an intimate-data product where the RLS layer is the entire privacy boundary shared by four clients, an accidental policy widening in a future migration would currently be caught by no automation.
findings.evidence: Covered set: packages/supabase/scripts/verify-pebble-drafts.ts:154-179, verify-pebble-visibility.ts (read matrix + write denial), verify-public-profile.ts (anon allowlist). Uncovered set derived from grep 'create table' over migrations (30 tables) and the 50-function definer inventory vs grep of scripts/ for each name. No pgTAP directory, no workflow invocation (grep .github/workflows returns nothing).
findings.remediation: Build a schema-driven denial suite (pgTAP, or extend the Deno harness pattern) that enumerates application tables and definer functions from information_schema at runtime, asserts cross-user select/insert/update/delete and anon access per table and non-owner refusal per RPC, and fails on any table/function without a registered expectation. Run it in CI on migration changes against a local supabase stack.

verification.note: Re-checked all four verify harnesses (packages/supabase/scripts/verify-{pebble-drafts,pebble-visibility,public-profile,account-purge}.ts), the RPC calls they make, the full migration inventory (~27 RLS-enabled tables, ~61 functions), and .github/workflows. The systemic claim holds on every load-bearing point: (1) no CI runs any DB harness (workflows are android-release, android, arkaik, lab-note-reminder; the verify scripts are not even wired as npm scripts, they are hand-run deno invocations needing remote env vars); (2) no completeness check diffs covered tables/RPCs against the schema; (3) no pgTAP or tests directory exists; (4) collections, karma_events, wallet_balances, bounces, glyph_submissions/entitlements/favourites, connections/connection_invites/connection_blocks, logs, log_reactions, and direct profiles selects have zero denial assertions; (5) no script ever invokes update_pebble, delete_pebble, remove_connection, spend_karma, or any admin_* function, so no refusal path is tested (the rpc inventory across scripts is only create_pebble, buy_glyph, check_achievements, get_public_profile, get_shared_pebble, set_handle, purge_account, and the connection-invite pair). Two evidence corrections that do not move the severity: the covered set is slightly larger than "3 of ~30" because verify-public-profile.ts:333-344 explicitly asserts cross-user AND anon denial on achievement_unlocks and anon denial on glyphs, and verify-pebble-visibility.ts:186-194 indirectly proves cross-user read denial on pebble_cards/souls/snaps through the security_invoker v_pebbles_full enrichment fence, so listing those five as uncovered is wrong; still ~19 tables and every mutating/admin RPC remain unproven. Aggravating factor: this failure class has already shipped twice in this repo, caught only manually: migration 20260729000000 documents #616 (definer-rights v_pebbles_full served 182 private pebbles across 20 users to the bare anon key) and cites the earlier v_ripple instance (20260516000001), which substantiates likelihood 3 and impact 4 exactly as reported.

findings.title: No CI gate exists for web: the 125-test vitest suite and the boundary-enforcing ESLint config never run on any PR or merge
findings.detail: The repository has exactly four workflows (android-release.yml, android.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml) and none references apps/web, so a PR that breaks any of the web tests or violates the lint-enforced data-layer boundary merges green by absence and auto-deploys via Vercel. The web suite exists precisely to pin cross-surface parity (the wobble golden asserts 1e-9 parity with the iOS fixture; settled-feed pins #700; flow.test pins the record flow contract), which is the class of silent-corruption bug the #651 postmortem documented (docs/decisions/log.md:316-323). The documented PR checklist compounds the hole: root CLAUDE.md step 5 says run lint/build at the scope of the change but never mentions running tests, so even a fully compliant contributor or agent ships without executing the suite. Shared-contract changes (packages/supabase migrations, generated types) also trigger zero client suites, so a schema change that breaks web decode paths runs nothing at all. Everything needed for the gate already exists and is green (baseline.md rows 1-2); only the workflow is missing.
findings.evidence: ls /home/user/pbbls/.github/workflows (4 files, none matching web); grep -rn 'apps/web|packages/supabase|migrations' .github/workflows/*.yml returns zero hits; /home/user/pbbls/turbo.json has no test task; /home/user/pbbls/apps/web/vercel.json is schema-only; docs/quality/audits/2026-08/baseline.md:8 confirms the suite passes when actually run; root CLAUDE.md PR checklist step 5 omits tests
findings.remediation: Add a web.yml workflow running 'npm run lint --workspace=apps/web' and 'npm run test --workspace=apps/web' on pull_request with paths covering apps/web/**, packages/supabase/** (types/migrations), and the workflow file itself; mark the job a required status check on main; add 'run the workspace test suite' to the PR checklist.

verification.note: Independently re-verified every evidence item: exactly 4 workflows exist, all path-filtered to apps/android/** or docs/arkaik/** (grep of on: blocks shows zero web/supabase paths); turbo.json has no test task and root package.json no test script; no husky/lefthook/pre-commit hooks; apps/web's vitest suite (12 files, 125 tests per baseline.md:8) includes wobble.golden.test.ts asserting 1e-9 parity against the iOS fixture, settled-feed.test.ts pinning #700, and flow.test.ts pinning the record-flow reducer; root CLAUDE.md PR checklist step 5 and the task-size triage both say lint/build only, never tests, and apps/web/CLAUDE.md lists npm run test only as an available command. Two aggravating factors found: (1) the repo ships Next 16 and its own vendored docs (node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/upgrading/version-16.md:1084) state 'next build no longer runs linting', so the Vercel deploy build cannot catch violations of the no-restricted-imports data-layer boundary in apps/web/eslint.config.mjs either — only type errors are caught; (2) the golden fixture lives in apps/ios/PebblesTests/Wobble/WobbleGolden.json and nothing in CI watches apps/ios/** at all, so an iOS-side fixture regeneration also merges without the web parity test ever running. Impact 4 x likelihood 3 is honest.

findings.title: French locale defaults to masculine forms addressing the user, including inside the emotion vocabulary itself
findings.detail: Multiple fr.json strings apply masculine participles to the user: connections.acceptedToast ('Te voilà connecté avec {name}'), record.flow.privacy.secret ('Toi seul peux le voir'), and a large share of the emotion catalog labels describe the user's state in masculine default ('Content d'un résultat', 'Déçu par des attentes non comblées', 'Épuisé émotionnellement', 'Se sentir fondamentalement défaillant', 'Comblé', 'Pris au dépourvu', 'Gêné', 'contrarié'). A woman or nonbinary French user picking an emotion at an emotionally vulnerable moment is addressed in the wrong gender by the core vocabulary of the product. The locale also mixes tu (37 strings) and vous (63 strings) with no guideline to arbitrate, and no written inclusive-copy guideline exists in the repo to prevent recurrence.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/i18n/messages/fr.json:135-136 area and the emotion.* namespace (emotion.satisfied.label, emotion.disappointed.label, emotion.drained.label, emotion.ashamed.label among others, dumped and reviewed in full); register counts from a script pass over all 829 fr keys; guideline absence: rg -i 'inclusive|tutoiement|vouvoiement' over docs/ and .claude/skills matches only the lab-note PR-note tone section.
findings.remediation: Write a short French inclusive-copy guideline (epicene constructions, chosen register), sweep fr.json rewriting masculine participles into nominal or epicene forms mirroring the EN labels' noun style ('Déception face à des attentes non comblées'), settle the tu/vous register once, and apply the same sweep to the iOS and Android string catalogs which mirror this vocabulary.

findings.title: No backup, export, or restore posture exists for the database, the two storage buckets, or auth identities
findings.detail: The repo contains no statement of what the hosted project's tier backs up, no retention or RPO/RTO numbers, no scheduled pg_dump or storage sync, no auth export, no restore procedure, and no rehearsal record. Whatever daily snapshots the platform tier includes, Supabase database backups do not cover storage objects, so users' photos in pebbles-media currently have no recovery path of any kind; auth users are likewise unverified. For a product whose entire value is irreplaceable personal history, an unrecoverable-loss event (platform incident, operator error against the linked project, a bad migration push) is the worst-case outcome, and GDPR Art. 32(1)(c) expects demonstrable restore ability. The strong migration and purge discipline elsewhere makes this the starkest gap on the surface: deletion is harness-verified, restoration is entirely unaddressed.
findings.evidence: Greps over docs/ and packages/supabase for backup, PITR, point-in-time, restore, retention return no infrastructure statements (only a /tmp colorset backup in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-17-ios-color-modifiers.md and Arkaik bundle backups); .github/workflows/ has no scheduled export job; buckets defined at 20260426000001_pebbles_pictures.sql:22-33 and 20260421000003_lab_assets_bucket.sql:9-11 appear in no coverage document
findings.remediation: Document the actual tier and its included backups first; add a scheduled workflow doing a logical dump plus a storage-object sync to independent storage with failure notification; execute one full restore to a scratch project including auth users and bucket objects, date it in docs, and put the rehearsal on a stated cadence.

findings.title: Admin changes merge green-by-absence: no CI workflow runs admin lint or build on any PR
findings.detail: The workflow set at the audit commit is android.yml, android-release.yml, arkaik.yml, and the advisory lab-note-reminder.yml. None has apps/admin (or packages/supabase, which admin's types depend on) in a path filter that runs an admin job, and the workspace has no test script for a future job to call. A PR that breaks admin's ESLint rules, its TypeScript build, or its compatibility with a schema change merges with zero checks executed; the first detection point is a post-merge Vercel build or an admin noticing the back-office broken. The baseline proves the gates exist and pass when run by hand (admin lint clean), so the entire gap is wiring, not tooling. Because moderation and Lab publishing run through this app, an undetected breakage stalls glyph review and release-note publishing until someone debugs main.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ contains only android-release.yml, android.yml, arkaik.yml, lab-note-reminder.yml (verified on the remote at commit 10181916 via GitHub contents API); android.yml on.pull_request.paths lists only apps/android/** and the workflow file; apps/admin/package.json:5-9 (no test script); docs/quality/audits/2026-08/baseline.md rows 'admin lint: clean' and 'admin tests: no test script exists'
findings.remediation: Add a web-admin.yml workflow running 'npm ci' plus 'npm run lint --workspace=apps/admin' and 'npm run build --workspace=apps/admin' with on.pull_request.paths covering apps/admin/**, packages/supabase/**, and the workflow file itself; make the job a required check on main.

findings.title: The drafts contract's proof machinery never grew an Android-shaped payload: harness and iOS foreign-payload tests cover only web and iOS shapes
findings.detail: Decision 2026-07-30 (#651) makes verify-pebble-drafts.ts the committed proof that pebble_drafts.payload survives every producer, and requires each surface to test against real payloads produced by the others. The harness fixtures cover an iosShaped payload (whole seconds, explicit nulls) and a webShaped payload (milliseconds); no androidShaped fixture exists, although Android became the third writer of the same contract (PebbleDraftsService.kt). Likewise iOS's DraftCrossSurfaceDecodingTests covers web-milliseconds, Postgres-microseconds and whole-seconds — never Android's actual emissions (seconds-less minute precision from pickers, non-UTC offsets, sub-second toString passthrough). The harness's own standing rule ('when the draft payload gains a key, add it to iosShaped') triggers on new keys but not on new surfaces, so the machinery stayed silent while the Android emission drifted out of the parseable set — which is exactly how the incompatibility in the previous finding shipped unseen. The iosShaped fixture has also drifted: it carries explicit nulls, which the iOS draft encoder (encodeIfPresent throughout) never writes — it is the create-payload shape, not what iOS drafts actually produce.
findings.evidence: packages/supabase/scripts/verify-pebble-drafts.ts:186-240 (iosShaped + webShaped only; no Android shape) and :28-29 (standing rule scoped to keys, not surfaces); apps/ios/PebblesTests/DraftCrossSurfaceDecodingTests.swift:12-32 (three fixtures, none Android-shaped); apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/pbbls/android/services/PebbleDraftsService.kt:74-81 (Android is a real third producer); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Path/Models/PebbleDraftPayload.swift:61-79 (encodeIfPresent — iOS drafts omit nulls, contradicting the fixture labeled iOS-shaped)
findings.remediation: Add an androidShaped fixture to verify-pebble-drafts.ts capturing Android's real emissions verbatim (minute-precision seconds-less timestamp, non-UTC offset, sub-second variant), add the same strings to iOS DraftCrossSurfaceDecodingTests and Android DraftCrossSurfaceDecodingTest, and extend the harness's standing-rule comment to trigger on new producing surfaces as well as new keys.

findings.title: SlideToConfirm purchase control is inoperable with TalkBack (label only, no action semantics)
findings.detail: The glyph purchase control is a custom drag-only slider whose accessibility surface is clearAndSetSemantics { contentDescription = a11y }. It exposes no onClick, no custom accessibility action, and no progress semantics, and the drag itself lives in a raw pointerInput that additionally requires the press to start on the 56dp thumb. A TalkBack user can hear the label but has no reliable way to activate the purchase: double-tap does nothing, and pass-through drag is undiscoverable and defeated by the thumb-origin check. The only karma-spending flow in the app is therefore closed to screen-reader users. iOS SlideToConfirm should be checked for the same gap under the mirror rule.
findings.evidence: apps/android/app/src/main/kotlin/app/pbbls/android/features/glyph/store/SlideToConfirm.kt:103 (clearAndSetSemantics with contentDescription only) and :104-130 (pointerInput drag with down.position.x > thumbPx early return); no customActions/onClick/progressSemantics in file
findings.remediation: Add a custom accessibility action (or onClick semantics) that performs the confirm directly when invoked via accessibility services, for example semantics { customActions = listOf(CustomAccessibilityAction(confirmLabel) { fire onConfirm; true }) }, keeping the drag as the pointer path.

findings.title: No VoiceOver pass has ever been recorded for the primary flows, and nothing automated asserts semantics
findings.detail: The labeling discipline in the code is real, but no end-to-end screen-reader verification exists: the Android parity audit states in writing that no accessibility pass has been done on either platform and TalkBack has never been validated on-device; iOS feature plans contain per-feature VoiceOver checklist steps but no recorded whole-flow pass; and the project policy is explicitly 'No UI tests for now', so no accessibility audit or semantics assertion runs anywhere. Concretely this means traversal order, focus traps in the 10-step record flow, and the announced experience of the custom Path timeline have never been observed with the screen reader on, and a regression (an unlabeled new control, a broken combine) would ship silently.
findings.evidence: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-android-parity-audit.md:147; apps/ios/CLAUDE.md ('No UI tests for now'); no accessibility-related test in apps/ios/PebblesTests (file listing reviewed); per-feature checkboxes only in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-19-ios-valence-picker.md:997-1009
findings.remediation: Run and record one VoiceOver pass over the primary flows (welcome/auth, record, path, read, settings/deletion) noting defects; longer term add an Xcode accessibility-audit test (performAccessibilityAudit) once a UI test target exists.

findings.title: The 125-test web Vitest suite and web ESLint run in no CI gate, and the PR checklist omits npm run test
findings.detail: No GitHub Actions workflow triggers on apps/web/** to run lint or tests; the only automated build of web is Vercel's deploy build, which does not execute vitest. The PR template checklist requires build and lint to pass but never mentions the test suite, so the one loop that is fast, green, and headless (1.15s at the snapshot) is exercised purely by agent discipline. Failure scenario: a PR touching pebble grouping or karma math lands with a broken unit test because the author ran only the checklist items; drift is discovered mid-task by the next agent whose local run goes red on code they did not write. Given the suite already exists and is fast, this is the cheapest unclaimed CI win in the repo.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ has no web job (ls); grep -rn 'vitest|npm run test' .github/ matches only copilot-instructions.md prose; .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:53-56 lists build and lint only; docs/quality/audits/2026-08/baseline.md:7-8
findings.remediation: Add a workflow path-filtered on apps/web/** running npm run lint --workspace=apps/web and npm run test --workspace=apps/web, and add a test line to the PR template checklist.

findings.title: Visibility enum decodes strictly with no unknown-case fallback, repeating the exact class of shipped bug #713
findings.detail: Visibility is a three-case raw-value Decodable enum decoded with a plain 'try container.decode' inside PebbleDetail. When the M51 backfill introduced the 'secret' value, the then two-case enum failed decoding and blanked the detail and edit sheets for every pebble (fixed in 6bf3f160 by adding the case, not by making the decode tolerant). The structural hazard is unchanged: the next visibility grade added by a migration or another surface before the iOS app updates will again make every PebbleDetail decode throw, and EditPebbleSheet.load()/PebbleDetailSheet will show 'Couldn't load this pebble.' for all affected rows. This contradicts both the repo's own tolerant-parsing discipline (applied to timestamps via ISO8601Flexible after #651) and the ARC-03 checklist requirement that unknown enum values decode to typed fallbacks.
findings.evidence: apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Path/Models/Visibility.swift:3-8 (enum Visibility: String... Decodable, no fallback case, no custom init(from:)); apps/ios/Pebbles/Features/Path/Models/PebbleDetail.swift:127 (try container.decode(Visibility.self...)); failure surface at Features/Path/EditPebbleSheet.swift:190-196; prior incident: commit 6bf3f160 message ('a two-case Visibility enum could not decode... blanking the detail and edit sheets for every pebble') and PebblesTests/PebbleDetailDecodingTests.swift:81-91.
findings.remediation: Give Visibility a tolerant decode (custom init(from:) mapping unknown raw values to a typed .unknown or to the most restrictive grade .secret, with a log), render unknown grades read-only, and add a foreign-payload test asserting a never-seen grade string still decodes.

findings.title: The create-or-replace re-emission collision remains manually policed even though it already fired once and the decision log names the next likely occurrence
findings.detail: Two migrations authored in parallel each re-emitted purge_account with only their own section-(4) append; the later timestamp won and silently dropped the other's three connections deletes — no VCS conflict, migration applied cleanly. The repair (manual union, in-body append markers, a documented pairwise-diff procedure) is exactly the l3 practice, but it is pure discipline: no script or CI step flags a batch containing two emissions of the same function name, and the decision log itself states that M52/M53 will append to both purge_account and remove_connection and 'are the next likely collision'.
